papers.abstract_zh: 背景:克罗恩病(CD)是一种胃肠道慢性炎症性疾病,其恶性肿瘤风险增加,尤其是在接受免疫抑制治疗的患者中。病例报告:本文描述了一位20岁女性患者被诊断为CD后,在长期使用硫唑嘌呤(AZA)治疗期间,先后发展出三种不同的癌变。该患者在使用AZA治疗3年后出现低级别宫颈上皮内瘤变(CIN 1;第10年),在治疗7年后(第14年)停用AZA 10个月后出现结膜鳞状细胞癌,以及在约9.2年累计AZA治疗后(第17年)出现皮肤基底细胞癌。在第18年,CD复发并重新开始AZA治疗,此时检测到CIN 2(约10.2年累计AZA治疗)。在第18年,AZA治疗被终止。不到一年(第19年),诊断出宫颈鳞状细胞癌。第23年时,CD得到控制,未见肿瘤记录。通过PCR检测到宫颈和结膜恶性肿瘤中存在高危型HPV16 DNA,并通过桑格测序确认。免疫组化分析显示高Ki-67和p16表达以及CD4+细胞占优,支持这些肿瘤与HPV16的关联。CIN 2与侵袭性宫颈鳞状细胞癌(CSCC)之间的时间间隔较短,这在临床上较为罕见。虽然这一时间点与慢性免疫抑制治疗重合,但目前尚无法直接推断因果关系;然而,患者的慢性免疫失调和免疫抑制可能为这些肿瘤的形成提供了贡献因素。结论:该病例突显了克罗恩病、长期免疫抑制治疗和HPV16感染在时间上的共存。这些发现强调了在慢性免疫抑制治疗期间对肠外癌症进行警惕性监测、定期筛查以及HPV 疫苗接种的重要性。局限性与证据强度:CIN 2与侵袭性CSCC之间的时间间隔较短,这在临床上较为罕见。虽然这一时间点与慢性免疫抑制治疗重合,但目前尚无法直接推断因果关系;然而,患者的慢性免疫失调和免疫抑制可能为这些肿瘤的形成提供了贡献因素。

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of E6/E7 mRNA Expression and Viral DNA Load in Cervical Lesions With Multiple High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Infection.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections are frequently detected in cervical screening, but their biological interactions and clinical significance remain unclear. Because HPV DNA detection indicates viral presence but not transcriptional activity, this exploratory study evaluated viral load, genotype-specific E6/E7 mRNA expression, localization, and follow-up. METHODS: Among 12 000 cervical specimens tested for hrHPV, 598 were positive and 72 showed multiple genotypes. Viral load was assessed using the BioPerfectus Multiplex Real-Time assay. A tissue-available subset of 36 dual HPV16 + 52 or HPV16 + 58 cases was analyzed by duplex RNAscope for genotype-specific E6/E7 mRNA expression and localization. Diagnoses were categorized as benign, low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL), or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL). Viral load and RNAscope analyses used incompletely matched subsets and were interpreted as complementary, not paired. RESULTS: Elevated viral load (≥4.00 log10 copies/10 000 cells) was associated with HSIL. In cohort-level analyses, diffuse (+++) E6/E7 mRNA expression was more frequent in HSIL than elevated viral load (95.2% vs 55.5%, P = .01). papers.title: High-risk HPV integration reprograms cis-regulatory architecture through HPV-specific stripe transcription factors
papers.abstract: Background: The integration of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) DNA into the host genome contributes to persistent viral infection and malignant progression in hrHPV-related carcinomas, but the integration-associated cis-regulatory programs remain incompletely defined, limiting the identification of potential therapeutic vulnerabilities.We aimed to characterize the regulatory architecture associated with hrHPV integration and evaluate its functional relevance in preclinical models.Methods: Human cervical epithelial organoids carrying integrated HPV16 upstream regulatory region-E6/E7 sequences and an HPV16-integrated mouse model (14 E2.2 HPV16-int ) were established.Viral integration mapping, motif enrichment analysis, chromatin accessibility and histone modification profiling, three-dimensional chromatin interaction analysis, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and patient-derived organoid/xenograft models were integrated to assess integration-associated regulatory changes and pharmacological perturbation.Results: Human epithelial organoids and mice with hrHPV integration recapitulated progressive malignant phenotypes in vitro and in vivo.Across cervical and head and neck cancer datasets, hrHPV integration hotspots were enriched for motifs of a defined subset of 25 HPV-specific stripe transcription factors (HSTFs).Higher HSTF motif density was associated with increased chromatin accessibility, active histone marks, enhanced super-enhancer-promoter interactions, and elevated HSTF regulatory activity along hrHPV-positive epithelial cancer trajectories.Spatial and single-cell multi-omic analyses further confirmed that HSTF activation was triggered by hrHPV integration, which could be blocked by HSTF inhibition in vivo.Conclusions: These findings reveal an hrHPV integration-associated cis-regulatory network that promotes chromatin remodeling and transcriptional activation in HPVdriven carcinogenesis.Targeting HSTF-associated regulatory program may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for hrHPV-integrated precancerous lesions and cancers.

papers.title_zh: 高危型HPV整合通过HPV特异性条带转录因子重新编程顺式调控架构
papers.source_body_en: Background: The integration of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) DNA into the host genome contributes to persistent viral infection and malignant progression in hrHPV-related carcinomas, but the integration-associated cis-regulatory programs remain incompletely defined, limiting the identification of potential therapeutic vulnerabilities.We aimed to characterize the regulatory architecture associated with hrHPV integration and evaluate its functional relevance in preclinical models.Methods: Human cervical epithelial organoids carrying integrated HPV16 upstream regulatory region-E6/E7 sequences and an HPV16-integrated mouse model (14 E2.2 HPV16-int ) were established.Viral integration mapping, motif enrichment analysis, chromatin accessibility and histone modification profiling, three-dimensional chromatin interaction analysis, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and patient-derived organoid/xenograft models were integrated to assess integration-associated regulatory changes and pharmacological perturbation.Results: Human epithelial organoids and mice with hrHPV integration recapitulated progressive malignant phenotypes in vitro and in vivo.Across cervical and head and neck cancer datasets, hrHPV integration hotspots were enriched for motifs of a defined subset of 25 HPV-specific stripe transcription factors (HSTFs).Higher HSTF motif density was associated with increased chromatin accessibility, active histone marks, enhanced super-enhancer-promoter interactions, and elevated HSTF regulatory activity along hrHPV-positive epithelial cancer trajectories.Spatial and single-cell multi-omic analyses further confirmed that HSTF activation was triggered by hrHPV integration, which could be blocked by HSTF inhibition in vivo.Conclusions: These findings reveal an hrHPV integration-associated cis-regulatory network that promotes chromatin remodeling and transcriptional activation in HPVdriven carcinogenesis.Targeting HSTF-associated regulatory program may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for hrHPV-integrated precancerous lesions and cancers.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:高危型人乳头瘤病毒(hrHPV)DNA整合到宿主 基因组中会促进hrHPV相关癌变中的持续病毒感染和恶性进展,但与整合相关的顺式调控程序仍不完全明确,限制了潜在治疗脆弱性的识别。我们旨在表征与hrHPV整合相关的调控架构,并评估其在临床前模型中的功能相关性。方法:建立了携带整合HPV16上游调控区-E6/E7序列的人类宫颈上皮类器官和一个HPV16整合的小鼠模型(14 E2.2 HPV16-int)。通过整合病毒整合图谱、基序富集分析、染色质可及性与组蛋白修饰分析、三维染色质相互作用分析、批量和单细胞转录组学、空间转录组学以及患者来源的类器官/异种移植模型,评估与hrHPV整合相关的调控变化和药物干预。结果:携带hrHPV整合的人类上皮类器官和小鼠在体外和体内均重现了逐渐恶化的恶性表型。在宫颈癌和头颈癌数据集中,hrHPV整合热点富含一组定义的25种HPV特异性条带转录因子(HSTFs)的基序。在hrHPV阳性上皮癌轨迹中,HSTF基序密度越高,染色质可及性、活跃的组蛋白标记、超级增强子-启动子相互作用以及HSTF调控活性均相应增强。空间和单细胞多组学分析进一步证实,HSTF的激活是由hrHPV整合触发的,这种激活可以在体内通过HSTF抑制被阻断。结论:这些发现揭示了与hrHPV整合相关的顺式调控网络,该网络促进染色质重塑和转录激活,从而推动HPV驱动的癌变。针对HSTF相关的调控程序可能代表一种治疗高危型HPV整合的癌前病变和癌症的有前景的策略。

papers.title: Presence of HPV infection, not age, identifies vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia: a 847-patient multivariable analysis with 40- and 45-year age-cutoff sensitivity testing
papers.abstract: Background Vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN) is a precursor of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma with two biologically distinct pathways: HPV-associated and HPV-independent disease. Whether chronological age is independently associated with VIN after adjusting for HPV infection and multifocal lower genital tract disease remains unclear. Methods ​We analyzed 847 women referred for colposcopy and vulvar evaluation between April 2022 and December 2025, including 568 VIN patients and 279 non-VIN controls. Univariable comparisons, age-stratified multivariable logistic regression (Enter method; complete-case n = 673), and sensitivity analyses using 40-year and 45-year cutoffs were performed. A further sensitivity analysis was restricted to high-grade lesions (HSIL/VIN2–3 vs. Results Univariable analysis showed that VIN patients were slightly younger (mean 39.66 ± 11.95 vs. 41.51 ± 12.52 years), more frequently asymptomatic, and had a higher HPV infection rate (80.2% vs. 55.7%, both P 0.05 at 40-year and 45-year cutoffs). At the 45-year cutoff, concurrent CIN was more frequent in the older group (12.2% vs. In the HSIL-only sensitivity analysis, continuous age remained non-significant (P = 0.492), while HPV infection was a strong independent risk factor (P 0.05). HPV infection was consistently and independently associated with VIN across all models (overall adjusted OR 3.146, P < 0.001; stratified aOR 2.812–3.859, all P < 0.001). Conclusions The marginal statistical significance of continuous age in the primary model reflects residual confounding by HPV infection and multifocal disease accumulation rather than an independent pathogenic role of chronological age. Vulvar inspection should be guided by HPV infection status and concurrent lower genital tract neoplasia rather than arbitrary age cutoffs, particularly given the high prevalence of asymptomatic VIN.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to determine whether HPV infection or age is more strongly associated with vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN), as VIN is a precursor of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma with two biologically distinct pathways: HPV-associated and HPV-independent disease.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multivariable analysis was conducted on 847 women referred for colposcopy and vulvar evaluation between April 2022 and December 2025, including 568 VIN patients and 279 non-VIN controls.
analysis.methods: Univariable comparisons, age-stratified multivariable logistic regression (Enter method; complete-case n = 673), and sensitivity analyses using 40-year and 45-year cutoffs were performed to assess the association between age, HPV infection, and VIN.
analysis.main_results: Univariable analysis showed VIN patients were slightly younger (mean 39.66 ± 11.95 vs. 41.51 ± 12.52 years), more frequently asymptomatic, and had a higher HPV infection rate (80.2% vs. 55.7%, both P < 0.05 at 40-year and 45-year cutoffs).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The marginal statistical significance of continuous age in the primary model reflects residual confounding by HPV infection and multifocal disease accumulation rather than an independent pathogenic role of chronological age.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that vulvar inspection should be guided by HPV infection status and concurrent lower genital tract neoplasia rather than arbitrary age cutoffs, particularly given the high prevalence of asymptomatic VIN.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's design, which included univariable comparisons and multivariable logistic regression, may have limitations in controlling for all confounding factors, but the evidence is strong given the consistent and independent association of HPV infection with VIN across all models.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between HPV infection and age with vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN), a precursor to vulvar squamous cell carcinoma. It analyzed 847 women, including 568 VIN patients and 279 non-VIN controls, using univariable comparisons, multivariable logistic regression, and sensitivity analyses with age cutoffs. The results showed VIN patients were younger and had a higher HPV infection rate compared to non-VIN controls. The marginal significance of age was attributed to residual confounding by HPV infection and multifocal disease. The study concluded that VIN should be identified by HPV infection status rather than age, emphasizing the need for HPV-focused screening. The findings have implications for clinical practice, suggesting that vulvar inspections should prioritize HPV testing and concurrent lower genital tract neoplasia detection over age-based criteria. The evidence is strong, but the study's design may limit its ability to fully control for confounding factors.

elements_en.study_design_and_population: A multivariable analysis was conducted on 847 women referred for colposcopy and vulvar evaluation between April 2022 and December 2025, including 568 VIN patients and 279 non-VIN controls.
elements_en.methods: Univariable comparisons, age-stratified multivariable logistic regression (Enter method; complete-case n = 673), and sensitivity analyses using 40-year and 45-year cutoffs were performed to assess the association between age, HPV infection, and VIN.
elements_en.main_results: Univariable analysis showed VIN patients were slightly younger (mean 39.66 ± 11.95 vs. 41.51 ± 12.52 years), more frequently asymptomatic, and had a higher HPV infection rate (80.2% vs. 55.7%, both P < 0.05 at 40-year and 45-year cutoffs).
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The marginal statistical significance of continuous age in the primary model reflects residual confounding by HPV infection and multifocal disease accumulation rather than an independent pathogenic role of chronological age.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that vulvar inspection should be guided by HPV infection status and concurrent lower genital tract neoplasia rather than arbitrary age cutoffs, particularly given the high prevalence of asymptomatic VIN.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's design, which included univariable comparisons and multivariable logistic regression, may have limitations in controlling for all confounding factors, but the evidence is strong given the consistent and independent association of HPV infection with VIN across all models.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在确定HPV感染或年龄与外阴上皮内瘤变(VIN)之间的关联强度,因为VIN是外阴鳞状细胞癌的前驱病变,具有两种生物学上不同的发病途径:HPV相关和HPV无关的疾病。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在2022年4月至2025年12月期间因阴道镜检查和外阴评估而就诊的847名女性中进行了多变量分析,其中包括568名VIN患者和279名非VIN对照组。
elements_zh.methods: 进行了单变量比较、按年龄分层的多变量逻辑回归分析(Enter方法;完整病例数n = 673)以及使用40岁和45岁分界点的敏感性分析,以评估年龄、HPV感染与VIN之间的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: 单变量分析显示VIN患者年龄略轻(平均39.66 ± 11.95岁 vs. 41.51 ± 12.52岁),更常无症状,且HPV感染率更高(80.2% vs. 55.7%,在40岁和45岁分界点时P均<0.05)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在主要模型中连续年龄的边缘统计学显著性反映了HPV感染和多灶性疾病积累的残留混杂因素,而非年龄本身的独立致病作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,外阴检查应依据HPV感染状态和并发的下生殖道肿瘤,而非随意的年龄分界点,特别是考虑到无症状VIN的高患病率。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究设计包括单变量比较和多变量逻辑回归分析,可能在控制所有混杂因素方面存在局限,但鉴于HPV感染在所有模型中均一致且独立地与VIN相关,证据是强有力的。

papers.title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染的存在而非年龄可识别外阴上皮内瘤变:一项847例患者的多变量分析及40岁和45岁年龄分界点敏感性检验
papers.source_body_en: Background Vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN) is a precursor of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma with two biologically distinct pathways: HPV-associated and HPV-independent disease. Whether chronological age is independently associated with VIN after adjusting for HPV infection and multifocal lower genital tract disease remains unclear. Methods ​We analyzed 847 women referred for colposcopy and vulvar evaluation between April 2022 and December 2025, including 568 VIN patients and 279 non-VIN controls. Univariable comparisons, age-stratified multivariable logistic regression (Enter method; complete-case n = 673), and sensitivity analyses using 40-year and 45-year cutoffs were performed. A further sensitivity analysis was restricted to high-grade lesions (HSIL/VIN2–3 vs. Results Univariable analysis showed that VIN patients were slightly younger (mean 39.66 ± 11.95 vs. 41.51 ± 12.52 years), more frequently asymptomatic, and had a higher HPV infection rate (80.2% vs. 55.7%, both P 0.05 at 40-year and 45-year cutoffs). At the 45-year cutoff, concurrent CIN was more frequent in the older group (12.2% vs. In the HSIL-only sensitivity analysis, continuous age remained non-significant (P = 0.492), while HPV infection was a strong independent risk factor (P 0.05). HPV infection was consistently and independently associated with VIN across all models (overall adjusted OR 3.146, P < 0.001; stratified aOR 2.812–3.859, all P < 0.001). Conclusions The marginal statistical significance of continuous age in the primary model reflects residual confounding by HPV infection and multifocal disease accumulation rather than an independent pathogenic role of chronological age. Vulvar inspection should be guided by HPV infection status and concurrent lower genital tract neoplasia rather than arbitrary age cutoffs, particularly given the high prevalence of asymptomatic VIN.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景 外阴上皮内瘤变(VIN)是外阴鳞状细胞癌的前驱病变,具有两种生物学上不同的发病途径:HPV相关和HPV无关的疾病。在调整了HPV感染和多灶性下生殖道疾病后,年龄是否独立与VIN相关仍不清楚。方法 我们分析了2022年4月至2025年12月期间因阴道镜检查和外阴评估而就诊的847名女性,包括568名VIN患者和279名非VIN对照组。进行了单变量比较、按年龄分层的多变量逻辑回归分析(Enter方法;完整病例数n = 673)以及使用40岁和45岁分界点的敏感性分析。在仅限于高危病变(HSIL/VIN2–3 vs. 结果 单变量分析显示VIN患者年龄略轻(平均39.66 ± 11.95岁 vs. 41.51 ± 12.52岁),更常无症状,且HPV感染率更高(80.2% vs. 55.7%,在40岁和45岁分界点时P均<0.05)。在45岁分界点时,老年组并发宫颈上皮内瘤变(CIN)的比例更高(12.2% vs. 在仅限于HSIL的敏感性分析中,连续年龄仍不显著(P = 0.492),而HPV感染是一个强的独立危险因素(P < 0.05)。HPV感染在所有模型中均一致且独立地与VIN相关(总体调整OR为3.146,P < 0.001;分层aOR为2.812–3.859,所有P < 0.001)。结论 在主要模型中连续年龄的边缘统计学显著性反映了HPV感染和多灶性疾病积累的残留混杂因素,而非年龄本身的独立致病作用。外阴检查应依据HPV感染状态和并发的下生殖道肿瘤,而非随意的年龄分界点,特别是考虑到无症状VIN的高患病率。

papers.title: Enhancing Human Papillomavirus Vaccine Communication with Mobile Health: Usability Insights from Caregivers and Health Care Providers.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite the effectiveness of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in preventing cancer, uptake remains suboptimal, especially among rural and underserved populations. Digital communication tools such as mobile health (mHealth) applications have the potential to improve access to accurate vaccine information and support shared decision-making. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the usability, acceptability, and perceived usefulness of a newly developed mHealth app for HPV vaccine communication in comparison to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC) HPV vaccine Web site. METHODS: Using a mixed-methods design and guided by the Health Belief Model and the mHealth Agile Development and Evaluation Lifecycle, caregivers, and health care providers were randomized to explore both the CDC Web site and the mHealth app in alternating order. Participants were asked to complete a session answering HPV vaccine questions with each tool and completed the mHealth App Usability Questionnaire, Propensity to Trust, and NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) after each session. Qualitative questions were asked after each session to capture additional feedback on items such as navigation and readability. Transcripts were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Quantitative results showed no difference between the tools in terms of being easy to use, requiring similar amounts of effort, and trust in the tool. Qualitative themes revealed that participants appreciated the app's streamlined navigation, tailored content, and readability. In contrast, the CDC Web site was seen as credible but often difficult to navigate, especially when searching for nuanced or specific vaccine information. CONCLUSION: Tailored mHealth tools developed with user-centered design principles may better meet the informational and usability needs of caregivers and health care providers compared with existing web-based resources. These findings support further development and integration of mHealth tools into vaccine communication strategies to enhance HPV vaccine communication.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:尽管人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)疫苗在预防癌症方面有效,但其接种率仍不理想,尤其是在农村和医疗资源不足的人群中。数字通信工具如移动健康(mHealth)应用程序有潜力改善获取准确疫苗信息的途径,并支持共同决策。研究目的:本研究旨在评估一种新开发的mHealth应用程序在与美国疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)的HPV 疫苗网站进行比较时的可用性、可接受性和感知有用性。研究方法:采用混合方法设计,依据健康信念模型和mHealth敏捷开发与评估生命周期,护理人员和医疗保健提供者被随机分配以交替顺序探索CDC网站和mHealth应用程序。参与者在使用每种工具回答HPV 疫苗相关问题后,完成了mHealth应用程序可用性问卷、信任倾向量表和NASA任务负荷指数(NASA-TLX)。在每次会话后,还通过定性问题收集关于导航和可读性的额外反馈。转录文本采用归纳主题分析法进行分析。研究结果:定量结果显示,两种工具在易用性、所需努力程度以及对工具的信任度方面没有显著差异。定性主题分析表明,参与者赞赏应用程序的简洁导航、定制内容和良好的可读性。相比之下,CDC网站被认为具有可信度,但在寻找细致或特定的疫苗信息时往往难以导航。研究结论:与现有的基于网络的资源相比,采用以用户为中心设计原则开发的定制mHealth工具可能更能满足护理人员和医疗保健提供者的信息和可用性需求。这些发现支持进一步开发和整合mHealth工具到疫苗沟通策略中,以增强HPV 疫苗的沟通效果。

papers.title: Presence of Human Papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr Virus in Breast Cancer Biopsies as Potential Risk Factors
papers.abstract: Introduction: Breast cancer represents the leading cause of cancer-related death in the Venezuelan female population.Many risk factors favoring its appearance have been reported; however, human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus have been associated in the past few decades as potential risk factors in the development of this malignancy.Objective: To detect the presence of human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus in breast cancer biopsies in order to establish a possible link between infection with these viral agents and the development of this pathology.Methods: Fresh biopsies were collected from patients with breast cancer and patients with breast benign pathology attending the Hospital Universitario de Caracas for surgery.Human papillomavirus detection was made using the INNO-LIPA ® HPV Genotyping Extra commercial kit (Innogenetics), and Epstein-Barr virus genome was detected with Epstein-Barr Virus BMLF1 commercial kit (Maxim Biotech, Inc.).Results: 63.6 and 13.6% of breast cancer cases were positive for human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus DNA, respectively, whereas the benign pathology samples had 4.5% positivity for each one of the viruses; 42.90% of breast cancer samples had mixed infection with low and high oncogenic risk human papillomavirus genotypes.Conclusion: We can suggest that human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus are important risk factors for breast cancer; however, studies allowing for the role of these viruses in the development of the disease to be elucidated are required.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Breast cancer represents the leading cause of cancer-related death in the Venezuelan female population. Many risk factors favoring its appearance have been reported; however, human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus have been associated in the past few decades as potential risk factors in the development of this malignancy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Fresh biopsies were collected from patients with breast cancer and patients with breast benign pathology attending the Hospital Universitario de Caracas for surgery.
analysis.methods: Human papillomavirus detection was made using the INNO-LIPA ® HPV Genotyping Extra commercial kit (Innogenetics), and Epstein-Barr virus genome was detected with Epstein-Barr Virus BMLF1 commercial kit (Maxim Biotech, Inc.).
analysis.main_results: 63.6 and 13.6% of breast cancer cases were positive for human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus DNA, respectively, whereas the benign pathology samples had 4.5% positivity for each one of the viruses; 42.90% of breast cancer samples had mixed infection with low and high oncogenic risk human papillomavirus genotypes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: We can suggest that human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus are important risk factors for breast cancer.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform future studies on the role of human papillomavirus in breast cancer development and highlight the need for further investigation into its potential as a risk factor.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the presence of human papillomavirus (HPV) and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) in breast cancer biopsies to determine their potential role as risk factors. The research is motivated by the fact that breast cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death in Venezuelan women, and previous associations between HPV and EBV and breast cancer have been noted. The study collected fresh biopsies from patients with breast cancer and those with benign pathology at the Hospital Universitario de Caracas. HPV was detected using the INNO-LIPA ® HPV Genotyping Extra commercial kit, while EBV was identified with the Epstein-Barr Virus BMLF1 commercial kit. Results showed that 63.6% of breast cancer cases were positive for HPV DNA, and 13.6% for EBV DNA, compared to 4.5% for each virus in benign samples. Additionally, 42.90% of breast cancer samples had mixed infections with low and high oncogenic risk HPV genotypes. The authors suggest that HPV and EBV may be important risk factors for breast cancer, though further studies are needed to clarify their role. The study's findings are limited by the lack of detailed limitations or evidence strength assessment.

elements_zh.main_results: 63.6和13.6%的乳腺癌病例分别对人乳头瘤病毒和Epstein-Barr病毒DNA呈阳性,而良性病理样本中每种病毒的阳性率均为4.5%;42.90%的乳腺癌样本存在低和高致癌风险的人乳头瘤病毒基因型混合感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 我们可以建议人乳头瘤病毒和Epstein-Barr病毒是乳腺癌的重要风险因素。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为未来研究人乳头瘤病毒在乳腺癌发展中的作用提供信息,并强调进一步研究其作为风险因素潜力的必要性。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Breast cancer represents the leading cause of cancer-related death in the Venezuelan female population. Many risk factors favoring its appearance have been reported; however, human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus have been associated in the past few decades as potential risk factors in the development of this malignancy.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: Fresh biopsies were collected from patients with breast cancer and patients with breast benign pathology attending the Hospital Universitario de Caracas for surgery.
analysis_en.methods: Human papillomavirus detection was made using the INNO-LIPA ® HPV Genotyping Extra commercial kit (Innogenetics), and Epstein-Barr virus genome was detected with Epstein-Barr Virus BMLF1 commercial kit (Maxim Biotech, Inc.).
analysis_en.main_results: 63.6 and 13.6% of breast cancer cases were positive for human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus DNA, respectively, whereas the benign pathology samples had 4.5% positivity for each one of the viruses; 42.90% of breast cancer samples had mixed infection with low and high oncogenic risk human papillomavirus genotypes.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: We can suggest that human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus are important risk factors for breast cancer.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform future studies on the role of human papillomavirus in breast cancer development and highlight the need for further investigation into its potential as a risk factor.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength.

papers.title_zh: 乳腺癌活检中人乳头瘤病毒和Epstein-Barr病毒的存在作为潜在风险因素
papers.source_body_en: Introduction: Breast cancer represents the leading cause of cancer-related death in the Venezuelan female population.Many risk factors favoring its appearance have been reported; however, human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus have been associated in the past few decades as potential risk factors in the development of this malignancy.Objective: To detect the presence of human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus in breast cancer biopsies in order to establish a possible link between infection with these viral agents and the development of this pathology.Methods: Fresh biopsies were collected from patients with breast cancer and patients with breast benign pathology attending the Hospital Universitario de Caracas for surgery.Human papillomavirus detection was made using the INNO-LIPA ® HPV Genotyping Extra commercial kit (Innogenetics), and Epstein-Barr virus genome was detected with Epstein-Barr Virus BMLF1 commercial kit (Maxim Biotech, Inc.).Results: 63.6 and 13.6% of breast cancer cases were positive for human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus DNA, respectively, whereas the benign pathology samples had 4.5% positivity for each one of the viruses; 42.90% of breast cancer samples had mixed infection with low and high oncogenic risk human papillomavirus genotypes.Conclusion: We can suggest that human papillomavirus and Epstein-Barr virus are important risk factors for breast cancer; however, studies allowing for the role of these viruses in the development of the disease to be elucidated are required.

papers.title: Post-Treatment Surveillance After Conisation for CIN2/3 in Norway: Long-Term CIN3+ Risk Stratification Comparing HPV DNA Testing with Cytology/HPV16/18/45 mRNA Co-Testing
papers.abstract: We compared surveillance strategies in a retrospective regional cohort of 2136 women who underwent conisation for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or 3 (CIN2/3) in 2016–2020. Using results from the first eligible visit 90–548 days after treatment, we evaluated cytology, human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA testing and HPV16/18/45 E6/E7 messenger RNA (mRNA) testing, individually and in combination. We also evaluated an exploratory referral strategy adapted from the Addressing the Need for Advanced HPV Diagnostics (ATHENA) study. Histological outcomes were ascertained through 2025. Median available administrative follow-up was 7.24 years. CIN3+ (CIN3, adenocarcinoma in situ or invasive cervical cancer) was recorded in 74 women (3.5%). For CIN3+, HPV DNA testing had 93.2% sensitivity, 78.0% specificity and 24.4% positivity. Adding mRNA positivity to high-grade+ cytology increased CIN3+ sensitivity from 60.8% to 82.4%, with 92.1% specificity and 10.4% test positivity. Combining ASC-US+ cytology with mRNA positivity achieved the highest observed CIN3+ sensitivity (95.9%), with 73.5% specificity. The ATHENA-derived strategy achieved 90.5% sensitivity and 83.1% specificity, with 19.4% classified as referral-positive. Among women with equivocal or low-grade cytology, CIN3+ was recorded in 18.6% with positive mRNA and 2.5% with negative mRNA. Cytology and genotype-specific mRNA co-testing may support risk stratification after conisation. Prospective evaluation is needed to establish safe surveillance intervals.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估不同锥切术后检测策略在识别宫颈上皮内瘤变2/3级(CIN2/3)长期CIN3+风险方面的有效性,以应对锥切术后改进风险分层方法的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对2016年至2020年间接受锥切术治疗CIN2/3的2136名女性进行了回顾性区域研究。组织学结果通过2025年确认,中位数行政随访时间为7.24年。

elements_zh.main_results: CIN3+在74名女性中被记录(3.5%)。HPV DNA检测的敏感性为93.2%,特异性为78.0%,阳性率为24.4%。将ASC-US+细胞学结果与mRNA阳性结果结合,达到了最高的观察到的CIN3+敏感性(95.9%),特异性为73.5%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,细胞学和基因型特异性mRNA联合检测可能有助于锥切术后风险分层,提供了一种更敏感的检测CIN3+的方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于制定更有效的锥切术后随访策略,以降低宫颈癌的长期风险,从而改善长期监测并减少漏诊的可能性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究为回顾性研究,缺乏前瞻性评估,这限制了所提出的锥切术后随访间隔的可信度。由于研究的观察性质和潜在偏倚,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Factors associated with biopsy-confirmed high-grade cervical lesions (CIN2+) in women undergoing colposcopy: role of HPV infection, vaccination status, and cytology
papers.abstract: Background High-grade cervical lesions (CIN2+) are important precursors of cervical cancer. HPV infection, cytological abnormalities, and HPV vaccination status may be associated with CIN2+. This study evaluated factors associated with biopsy-confirmed CIN2 + in women undergoing colposcopy, with particular focus on HPV infection and vaccination status. Methods In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 246 women undergoing colposcopy, from January 2014 to January 2024 were included. HPV was detected using the PaxView ® Kit. CIN2 + was defined as histopathologically confirmed CIN2, CIN3, adenocarcinoma in situ, or invasive cervical cancer. HPV status, vaccination status, cytology, and clinical characteristics were assessed. Univariable and multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with CIN2+. adjusted odds ratios (aOR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated. Results Among 246 women included in the analysis, 50 (20.3%) had biopsy-confirmed CIN2+, including 37 (74.0%) with CIN2, 10 (20.0%) with CIN3, 2 (4.0%) with adenocarcinoma in situ, and 1 (2.0%) with invasive cervical cancer. HPV status and cytological findings differed significantly between women with CIN2 + and CIN2− (both p < 0.001). HPV16/18 was more frequent among women with CIN2 + than CIN2− (56.0% vs. 28.6%), whereas HPV-negative results were less frequent (18.0% vs. Similarly, HSIL cytology (38.0% vs. 10.7%) and lack of HPV vaccination (42.0% vs. 16.8%) were more common in the CIN2 + group. In multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression, HPV16/18 infection (aOR, 3.94; 95% CI, 1.70–9.74; p = 0.001), lack of HPV vaccination (aOR, 2.20; 95% CI, 1.03–4.65; p = 0.042), and HSIL cytology compared with NILM (aOR, 2.84; 95% CI, 1.09–7.54; p = 0.031) were independently associated with CIN2+. Age, marital status and other high-risk HPV genotypes were not significantly associated with CIN2+. Conclusion In this Iranian colposcopy population, HPV16/18 infection and HSIL cytology were independently associated with biopsy-confirmed CIN2+. Lack of HPV vaccination was also associated with higher odds of CIN2+, but this finding should be interpreted cautiously, as the timing of vaccination relative to HPV exposure was not recorded and the association may reflect unmeasured confounding parameters. Prospective studies focusing on vaccination timing and pre-vaccination HPV status are needed to clarify this association.

papers.title: Immediate Risk of Cervical Precancer and Primary Triage Strategies for Women with Non- 16/18 High-Risk HPV Infection and ASC-US/LSIL Cytology: A Real-World Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective We evaluated the immediate risk of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) conferred by non-16/18 high-risk HPV (hrHPV) genotypes in women with atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US) and low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL) cytology, and developed a risk-based primary triage strategy. We also characterized the regional epidemiological features of HPV infection in Ningbo, China, from 2019 to 2024. Methods Based on defined eligibility criteria, this study enrolled 511,133 women participating in cervical cancer screening in Ningbo from 2019 to 2024. Colposcopy and histopathological biopsy were performed based on HPV and liquid-based cytology (TCT) findings. We used lowest-attribution (minimum), any-attribution, and hierarchical-attribution models to evaluate the distribution of non-16/18 hrHPV genotypes and their immediate risks of progressing to CIN2 + under ASC-US and LSIL cytology. Finally, we formulated a risk-stratified clinical triage framework by integrating recent evidence on extended HPV genotyping. Results Of 511,133 women screened, 50,320 (9.84%) were HPV-positive, with HPV52, 58, and 16 identified as the predominant genotypes. Non-16/18 hrHPV accounted for 84.18% (42,357/50,320) of all HPV-positive cases. Across both ASC-US and LSIL cytology, HPV31 conferred the highest immediate risk of CIN2 + among all non-16/18 genotypes. Conclusion Although non-16/18 hrHPV genotypes predominate among HPV-positive women, their immediate risks of CIN2 + are highly heterogeneous. A uniform management protocol for managing non-16/18 hrHPV infections wastes medical resources. We propose a three-tiered, extended genotyping-based triage strategy for women with ASC-US/LSIL cytology: direct colposcopy for high-risk genotypes (HPV31, 33, 52, and 58); conservative follow-up for low-risk genotypes (HPV39, 56, 66, and 68); and secondary triage using biomarkers (e.g., DNA methylation, p16/Ki-67 dual staining) or cytology for intermediate-risk genotypes. This framework is designed for initial, immediate triage and does not replace long-term longitudinal surveillance for specific genotypes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the immediate risk of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) conferred by non-16/18 high-risk HPV genotypes in women with ASC-US and LSIL cytology, and to develop a risk-based primary triage strategy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This real-world cross-sectional study enrolled 511,133 women participating in cervical cancer screening in Ningbo, China, from 2019 to 2024, focusing on those with ASC-US and LSIL cytology.
analysis.methods: The study used lowest-attribution, any-attribution, and hierarchical-attribution models to assess the distribution of non-16/18 hrHPV genotypes and their immediate risks of progressing to CIN2+ under ASC-US and LSIL cytology.
analysis.main_results: Of the 511,133 women screened, 50,320 (9.84%) were HPV-positive, with HPV52, 58, and 16 being the predominant genotypes. Non-16/18 hrHPV accounted for 84.18% (42,357/50,320) of all HPV-positive cases.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that non-16/18 hrHPV genotypes have highly heterogeneous immediate risks of CIN2+ and proposed a three-tiered, extended genotyping-based triage strategy for women with ASC-US/LSIL cytology.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of a risk-stratified clinical triage framework for managing HPV infections in women with ASC-US/LSIL cytology, potentially improving resource allocation and patient outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and the lack of longitudinal data, which may affect the interpretation of immediate risk. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immediate risk of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) associated with non-16/18 high-risk HPV genotypes in women with ASC-US and LSIL cytology, and developed a risk-based triage strategy. Conducted in Ningbo, China, from 2019 to 2024, the cross-sectional study enrolled 511,133 women, with 50,320 testing HPV-positive. Non-16/18 hrHPV accounted for 84.18% of all HPV-positive cases, and HPV31 was identified as the highest risk genotype. The authors proposed a three-tiered triage strategy based on extended genotyping, recommending direct colposcopy for high-risk genotypes, conservative follow-up for low-risk genotypes, and secondary triage using biomarkers or cytology for intermediate-risk genotypes. The study highlights the heterogeneity of risk among non-16/18 hrHPV genotypes and suggests a more tailored approach to triage. However, the cross-sectional design limits the ability to infer causality or long-term outcomes, resulting in moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the immediate risk of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) conferred by non-16/18 high-risk HPV genotypes in women with ASC-US and LSIL cytology, and to develop a risk-based primary triage strategy.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This real-world cross-sectional study enrolled 511,133 women participating in cervical cancer screening in Ningbo, China, from 2019 to 2024, focusing on those with ASC-US and LSIL cytology.
analysis_en.methods: The study used lowest-attribution, any-attribution, and hierarchical-attribution models to assess the distribution of non-16/18 hrHPV genotypes and their immediate risks of progressing to CIN2+ under ASC-US and LSIL cytology.
analysis_en.main_results: Of the 511,133 women screened, 50,320 (9.84%) were HPV-positive, with HPV52, 58, and 16 being the predominant genotypes. Non-16/18 hrHPV accounted for 84.18% (42,357/50,320) of all HPV-positive cases.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that non-16/18 hrHPV genotypes have highly heterogeneous immediate risks of CIN2+ and proposed a three-tiered, extended genotyping-based triage strategy for women with ASC-US/LSIL cytology.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of a risk-stratified clinical triage framework for managing HPV infections in women with ASC-US/LSIL cytology, potentially improving resource allocation and patient outcomes.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and the lack of longitudinal data, which may affect the interpretation of immediate risk. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

papers.title_zh: ASC-US/LSIL细胞学中非16/18型高危型人乳头瘤病毒感染与宫颈高级别上皮内瘤变的即时风险及初级分流策略:一项真实世界横断面研究
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Objective We evaluated the immediate risk of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) conferred by non-16/18 high-risk HPV (hrHPV) genotypes in women with atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US) and low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL) cytology, and developed a risk-based primary triage strategy. We also characterized the regional epidemiological features of HPV infection in Ningbo, China, from 2019 to 2024. Methods Based on defined eligibility criteria, this study enrolled 511,133 women participating in cervical cancer screening in Ningbo from 2019 to 2024. Colposcopy and histopathological biopsy were performed based on HPV and liquid-based cytology (TCT) findings. We used lowest-attribution (minimum), any-attribution, and hierarchical-attribution models to evaluate the distribution of non-16/18 hrHPV genotypes and their immediate risks of progressing to CIN2 + under ASC-US and LSIL cytology. Finally, we formulated a risk-stratified clinical triage framework by integrating recent evidence on extended HPV genotyping. Results Of 511,133 women screened, 50,320 (9.84%) were HPV-positive, with HPV52, 58, and 16 identified as the predominant genotypes. Non-16/18 hrHPV accounted for 84.18% (42,357/50,320) of all HPV-positive cases. Across both ASC-US and LSIL cytology, HPV31 conferred the highest immediate risk of CIN2 + among all non-16/18 genotypes. Conclusion Although non-16/18 hrHPV genotypes predominate among HPV-positive women, their immediate risks of CIN2 + are highly heterogeneous. A uniform management protocol for managing non-16/18 hrHPV infections wastes medical resources. We propose a three-tiered, extended genotyping-based triage strategy for women with ASC-US/LSIL cytology: direct colposcopy for high-risk genotypes (HPV31, 33, 52, and 58); conservative follow-up for low-risk genotypes (HPV39, 56, 66, and 68); and secondary triage using biomarkers (e.g., DNA methylation, p16/Ki-67 dual staining) or cytology for intermediate-risk genotypes. This framework is designed for initial, immediate triage and does not replace long-term longitudinal surveillance for specific genotypes.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 目的 我们评估了在ASC-US(意义未明的非典型鳞状细胞)和LSIL(低级别鳞状上皮内病变)细胞学检查的女性中,非16/18型高危型人乳头瘤病毒(hrHPV)基因型对宫颈高级别上皮内瘤变(CIN2+)的即时风险,并制定了基于风险的初级分流策略。我们还描述了2019年至2024年间中国宁波地区人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染的流行病学特征。方法 根据定义的纳入标准,本研究纳入了2019年至2024年期间参与宁波宫颈癌筛查的511,133名女性。根据HPV和液基细胞学(TCT)检查结果进行阴道镜检查和组织病理学活检。我们使用最低归因、任意归因和分层归因模型来评估非16/18型hrHPV基因型的分布及其在ASC-US和LSIL细胞学检查下进展为CIN2+的即时风险。最后,我们通过整合最新的扩展HPV基因型证据,制定了一个基于风险的临床分流框架。结果 在511,133名接受筛查的女性中,有50,320名(9.84%)HPV阳性,其中HPV52、58和16是主要的基因型。非16/18型hrHPV占所有HPV阳性病例的84.18%(42,357/50,320)。在ASC-US和LSIL细胞学检查中,HPV31在所有非16/18型基因型中对CIN2+的即时风险最高。结论 尽管非16/18型hrHPV基因型在HPV阳性女性中占主导地位,但它们进展为CIN2+的即时风险高度异质。对非16/18型hrHPV感染采用统一的管理方案会浪费医疗资源。我们提出了一种三级、基于扩展基因型的分流策略,用于ASC-US/LSIL细胞学检查的女性:对高风险基因型(HPV31、33、52和58)直接进行阴道镜检查;对低风险基因型(HPV39、56、66和68)采取保守随访;对中等风险基因型则使用生物标志物(如DNA甲基化、p16/Ki-67双染色)或细胞学进行二次分流。该框架旨在进行初始的即时分流,不替代特定基因型的长期纵向监测监测。

papers.title: High-risk human papillomavirus detection across the cervical disease spectrum in Abuja, Nigeria: a comparative cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major public health problem in Nigeria, yet data on high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) across the cervical disease spectrum are limited in Abuja. We conducted a hospital-based comparative cross-sectional study of 101 women aged [≥]25 years at Federal Medical Centre, Abuja: 59 with negative cytology (NILM) and 42 with cervical lesions, comprising 23 low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL), 8 high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL), and 11 invasive cervical cancers. Cervical specimens were tested using the Atila ScreenFire assay, which reports four pooled hrHPV target groups. hrHPV DNA was detected in 37/101 women (36.6%): 30.5% (18/59) with NILM, 26.1% (6/23) with LSIL, 50.0% (4/8) with HSIL, and 81.8% (9/11) with invasive cervical cancer (Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact p=0.005). Compared with NILM, invasive cervical cancer was associated with approximately tenfold higher odds of hrHPV detection (unadjusted odds ratio [OR] 10.25, 95% CI 2.01-52.28; age-adjusted OR 9.90, 95% CI 1.87-52.38). The HPV31/33/35/52/58 target group was detected most frequently overall (12.9%), followed by HPV16 and HPV18/45 (10.9% each), and HPV39/51/56/59/68 (5.9%). HPV16 was the most frequent target group in invasive cervical cancer (5/11). No individual target group was independently associated with lesion status. The NILM and lesion groups differed substantially in ethnicity, religion, and previous cervical screening, indicating different referral and screening pathways; therefore, the NILM group should not be considered population-based. These findings demonstrate marked enrichment of hrHPV in invasive cervical cancer and substantial detection of non-16/18 target groups. They support HPV-based screening, continued genotype surveillance, and larger multicentre studies using population-based comparison groups.

papers.title: Differential effect of obesity on cervical neoplastic progression and human papillomavirus persistence: A retrospective cohort study
papers.abstract: The role of obesity in human papillomavirus (HPV) persistence and the development of cervical neoplasia remains incompletely understood. This study evaluates the independent effects of obesity, smoking, and age on high-risk HPV persistence and the development of high-grade cervical lesions (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia [CIN]2+), and assesses whether obesity improves prediction of CIN2+. This retrospective cohort study included 445 women who underwent high-risk HPV testing between December 2023 and December 2025. HPV persistence was defined as detection of the same HPV genotype in at least two consecutive tests performed ≥ 12 months apart. Body mass index was categorized as non-obese (<30 kg/m2) or obese (≥30 kg/m2). Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent determinants of HPV persistence and CIN2+. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis was used to compare a baseline model including age and smoking with an extended model additionally including obesity. Persistent HPV infection was identified in 59 women (13.3%). Smoking was a strong independent predictor of HPV persistence (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 13.07; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 6.54–26.09; p < 0.001), and increasing age was also independently associated with persistence (aOR: 1.04 per year; 95% CI: 1.01–1.07; p = 0.023). Obesity was not independently associated with HPV persistence. CIN2+ was detected in 95 women (21.3%). Obesity was independently associated with CIN2+ (aOR: 1.96; 95% CI: 1.14–3.38; p = 0.015), whereas smoking and age were not significant predictors. The addition of obesity modestly improved discrimination for CIN2+ prediction (area under the curve [AUC] 0.545 vs. Smoking and age are key determinants of HPV persistence, whereas obesity appears to be associated primarily with cervical neoplastic progression rather than viral persistence. The modest increase in AUC suggests limited but measurable predictive contribution of obesity to CIN2+ risk.

papers.title_zh: 肥胖对宫颈癌前病变进展和人乳头瘤病毒持续性的影响差异:一项回顾性队列研究研究
papers.source_body_en: The role of obesity in human papillomavirus (HPV) persistence and the development of cervical neoplasia remains incompletely understood. This study evaluates the independent effects of obesity, smoking, and age on high-risk HPV persistence and the development of high-grade cervical lesions (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia [CIN]2+), and assesses whether obesity improves prediction of CIN2+. This retrospective cohort study included 445 women who underwent high-risk HPV testing between December 2023 and December 2025. HPV persistence was defined as detection of the same HPV genotype in at least two consecutive tests performed ≥ 12 months apart. Body mass index was categorized as non-obese (<30 kg/m2) or obese (≥30 kg/m2). Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent determinants of HPV persistence and CIN2+. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis was used to compare a baseline model including age and smoking with an extended model additionally including obesity. Persistent HPV infection was identified in 59 women (13.3%). Smoking was a strong independent predictor of HPV persistence (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 13.07; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 6.54–26.09; p < 0.001), and increasing age was also independently associated with persistence (aOR: 1.04 per year; 95% CI: 1.01–1.07; p = 0.023). Obesity was not independently associated with HPV persistence. CIN2+ was detected in 95 women (21.3%). Obesity was independently associated with CIN2+ (aOR: 1.96; 95% CI: 1.14–3.38; p = 0.015), whereas smoking and age were not significant predictors. The addition of obesity modestly improved discrimination for CIN2+ prediction (area under the curve [AUC] 0.545 vs. Smoking and age are key determinants of HPV persistence, whereas obesity appears to be associated primarily with cervical neoplastic progression rather than viral persistence. The modest increase in AUC suggests limited but measurable predictive contribution of obesity to CIN2+ risk.

supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 21, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer Rural Kerala Screening Detects Diverse Non-Vaccine High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Strains by November 20, 2026 in Cancer Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Rural Kerala Screening Detects Diverse Non-Vaccine High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Strains Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A community-based cervical screening investigation across rural and tribal regions of Kerala, India, has detected circulating high-risk human papillomavirus genotypes that include strains not covered by current prophylactic vaccines. The study, conducted by researchers Anusha M. Sharma, Sachin David, Parasmal Suresh, Sivadas Swathi Krishna, Neethu Puthalon Kunnath, Beena Karimbuvayalil Vasudevan, Lalitha Biswas, and Keechilat Pavithran, evaluated 358 women residing in underserved localities of the Idukki district. Among the screened cohort, real-time polymerase chain reaction assays and subsequent genetic sequencing identified high-risk human papillomavirus in 2.23 percent of participants, corresponding to eight positive individuals. Notably, while the established carcinogenic type HPV16 accounted for a portion of the positive findings, the researchers observed a notable variety of non-vaccine high-risk genotypes, uncovering localized viral profiles that provide foundational baseline data for regional public health evaluations and future preventive strategies. Cervical cancer represents a substantial global public health challenge, ranking as the fourth most common cancer among women worldwide, with approximately 660,000 new cases and 350,000 deaths recorded in 2022. Nearly 94 percent of these fatal outcomes occur within low- and middle-income nations, underscoring pronounced international disparities regarding access to early screening programs, diagnostic interventions, and prophylactic vaccination. Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus constitutes the established primary etiological driver of cervical malignant neoplasms. In India, cervical malignancy is the second most common cancer among women, responsible for an estimated 127,526 new diagnoses and 79,906 deaths annually according to GLOBOCAN 2022 statistics. The nationwide burden accounts for 6 to 29 percent of all female cancers, accompanied by striking regional variations and elevated disease incidence across rural territories where healthcare infrastructure and routine screening remain severely constrained. Epidemiological assessments indicate that annual cervical cancer incidence rates across India fluctuate markedly between 4.9 and 27.7 cases per 100,000 women, with particularly heightened burdens observed in northeastern areas as well as parts of southern and central regions. Infection rates in the general female population similarly exhibit wide geographic heterogeneity, spanning from approximately 10 percent in specific western and southern locales to upwards of 60 percent across sections of eastern India. Although multi-centre national investigations have documented that HPV16 and HPV18 together account for 74 to 78 percent of cervical cancer cases throughout India, other oncogenic viral types such as HPV33, HPV35, HPV45, and HPV58 contribute significantly depending on the local geographical context. In an earlier community assessment conducted on Vypeen Island in Kerala, researchers documented a 2 percent high-risk human papillomavirus prevalence characterized predominantly by HPV16 and HPV33, emphasizing the necessity of gathering targeted surveillance data from isolated settlements. Discover more Research assistant services Learn Engineering Track Biotech Tour Colleges Cancer research funding To address persistent knowledge gaps concerning viral circulation in remote regions, the research team organized institutional outreach screening camps across six rural and tribal villages within Kerala’s Idukki district: Kumily, Vandiperiyar, Marayoor, Devikulam, Mankulam, and Kanthalloor. These hospital-led initiatives were specifically structured to provide free cervical cancer screening and clinical counselling to underserved demographics lacking routine medical services. A total of 358 voluntary participants aged 30 years and older were enrolled, encompassing both asymptomatic individuals and symptomatic attendees seeking general health examinations. Demographic characterization revealed that women aged 35 to 45 years and 45 to 55 years constituted 70 percent of the total enrolled cohort. Cervical cellular specimens were collected by trained healthcare practitioners utilizing specialized brushes and EziPrep collection vials, followed by immediate cold storage at 4 degrees Celsius and prompt transfer to laboratory freezers maintained at minus 20 degrees Celsius. Genomic deoxyribonucleic acid was isolated from the preserved cervical samples within three to five days of collection using commercial QIAamp extraction kits. Initial molecular screening was performed using the QIAscreen real-time PCR assay on a Rotorgene Q system, which evaluates high-risk viral activity by targeting the conserved E7 gene across 15 high-risk genotypes, including HPV16, HPV18, HPV31, HPV33, HPV35, HPV39, HPV45, HPV51, HPV52, HPV56, HPV58, HPV59, HPV66, HPV67, and HPV68. The diagnostic workflow utilized multiplex four-reporter fluorophores, simultaneously tracking human beta-globin internal control integrity, HPV16, HPV18, and a composite pool of the 13 remaining high-risk strains. Cycle quantification thresholds verified sample validity and viral presence, establishing positive diagnostic cutoffs below 36 cycles for types 16 and 18, and below 33.5 cycles for the pooled hrHPV channel, alongside strict beta-globin verification requirements. Discover more Donate to Research Find Conferences Health Among the 358 screened individuals, eight specimens produced positive real-time PCR outcomes for high-risk human papillomavirus, establishing an overall prevalence of 2.23 percent with an exact Clopper-Pearson 95 percent confidence interval spanning from 0.97 percent to 4.34 percent. Within these eight detected cases, two infections were identified specifically as HPV16 through genotype-specific real-time PCR amplification. Notably, HPV18 was not detected in any participant throughout the study population. The remaining six positive cervical specimens fell into the pooled high-risk category and required comprehensive Sanger sequencing for definitive genotype resolution. To achieve precise strain characterization, researchers amplified a 450-base-pair segment of the viral L1 structural gene using consensus degenerate primers MY09 and MY11. Sequence alignment via BLAST interrogation against reference databases identified the presence of HPV31, two distinct occurrences of HPV35, HPV45, HPV66, and HPV70, demonstrating that non-vaccine strains predominated among the positive findings. Phylogenetic reconstructions grounded in the sequenced partial L1 gene regions confirmed the evolutionary relationships between the Kerala viral isolates and globally circulating human papillomavirus lineages. Using the maximum likelihood estimation method combined with the Kimura two-parameter substitution model and 100 bootstrap replicates in MEGA version 11 software, the investigators demonstrated that the recovered isolates clustered closely with verified international reference strains, indicating high genetic sequence conservation rather than novel divergence. The Kerala HPV31 and HPV35 isolates clustered alongside reference strains reported from the United States, China, Brazil, and Luxembourg with 97 percent and 99 percent bootstrap support. The HPV45 isolate grouped with counterparts from China and Luxembourg at 96 percent bootstrap confidence, while HPV66 showed 100 percent alignment with globally distributed reference sequences, and HPV70 resolved into a clade containing Brazilian, Togolese, and Chinese strains with 85 percent bootstrap support. The identification of HPV66 and HPV70 in this rural Kerala cohort is of particular epidemiological interest because neither genotype is targeted by existing bivalent, quadrivalent, or nonavalent prophylactic vaccines. While bivalent formulations cover HPV16 and HPV18, and nonavalent immunizations protect against seven oncogenic variants including types 16, 18, 31, 33, 45, 52, and 58, they exclude HPV66 and HPV70 entirely. HPV66 is classified as a possibly carcinogenic agent with documented involvement in cervical lesions, for which cross-protective immunity remains doubtful. HPV70, traditionally categorized as a probable high-risk strain, has increasingly been detected in high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia and invasive squamous cell carcinoma, presenting negligible likelihood of vaccine cross-protection due to its phylogenetic divergence from vaccine-included strains. Furthermore, although HPV35 has recognized oncogenic associations, it is not directly formulated into current vaccines, and documented cross-protection conferred by bivalent vaccines remains incomplete and waning over time. The detection of HPV45 in an HIV-negative rural Indian population also carries notable epidemiological significance, given that this recognized oncogenic genotype is more frequently documented as a predominant driver of cervical malignancy in sub-Saharan African settings. While HPV45 is incorporated within modern multivalent prophylactic vaccine formulations, its observed occurrence in southern India underscores the necessity of continuous molecular surveillance to observe how localized viral distributions align with immunization policies over time. The overall 2.23 percent prevalence observed in Idukki closely matches the 2 percent infection rate identified in the team’s prior community assessment on Vypeen Island, contrasting sharply with hospital-based Indian investigations from Bihar and Andhra Pradesh that report prevalence figures between 37.3 percent and 86.7 percent due to the inclusion of symptomatic patients and individuals presenting with active cervical lesions. The study authors acknowledged several important methodological limitations inherent to the investigation’s cross-sectional framework. The total sample cohort was limited to 358 voluntary participants across six rural villages, which restricts the direct generalizability of the epidemiological findings to the broader female population of Kerala or other diverse territories across India. The single-timepoint cross-sectional sampling captures only a momentary snapshot of viral presence and genotype distribution, precluding longitudinal evaluation of infection clearance, viral persistence, or clinical progression toward precancerous cervical intraepithelial lesions. Furthermore, recruitment through voluntary community medical camps carries inherent selection bias, as attendees may possess differing health-seeking motivations compared to the non-screened population. Finally, Sanger sequencing of consensus L1 amplicons preferentially amplifies dominant viral strains, meaning underlying minor co-infections cannot be entirely ruled out despite no mixed profiles being identified. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 21, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer Mekong Delta Study Finds Low HPV Prevalence Led by HPV52 and HPV58 by November 17, 2026 in Cancer Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Mekong Delta Study Finds Low HPV Prevalence Led by HPV52 and HPV58 Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram An unweighted human papillomavirus prevalence of 7.1 percent was observed among ever-married women aged 25 to 65 years in a community-based cross-sectional study conducted in Ca Mau Province, Vietnam. Published in Infectious Agents and Cancer, the investigation identified HPV52 and HPV58 as the most frequently detected genotypes across the cohort. Furthermore, among participants carrying an International Agency for Research on Cancer Group 1 carcinogenic genotype, nearly four in five women harbored neither HPV16 nor HPV18. The investigation addressed an important information gap in southern Vietnam, where community-based HPV genotype data remain limited. In this part of the Mekong Delta, local screening programmes face the practical challenge of interpreting genotype-specific risk in a population with low documented HPV vaccination. To provide empirical evidence for this setting, the researchers described overall HPV prevalence, the distribution of carcinogenic genotypes designated as Group 1 by the International Agency for Research on Cancer, infection multiplicity, woman-level detection of HPV16 and HPV18, and woman-level detection of at least one genotype included in the nonavalent vaccine. Fieldwork was conducted between January and June 2026 across Ca Mau Province. The research team utilized a three-stage sampling design with random selection procedures to recruit ever-married women between the ages of 25 and 65 years. From an eligible response-rate denominator of 1,565 women, a total of 1,193 women enrolled in the study, yielding a response rate of 76.2 percent. Because stage-specific selection probabilities were unavailable from the sampling process, the researchers reported all prevalence estimates as unweighted descriptive proportions for the enrolled cohort. Cervical cytology was performed concurrently alongside the molecular diagnostic testing. To convey the precision of their findings, the authors presented crude proportions accompanied by Wilson 95 percent confidence intervals calculated under the assumption of simple random sampling. In accordance with the descriptive scope of the study, the investigators did not perform inferential statistical comparisons among subgroups or genotype categories. The crude, unweighted HPV prevalence across the sample was 7.1 percent, representing 85 positive women out of the 1,193 enrolled participants, with a Wilson 95 percent confidence interval ranging from 5.8 percent to 8.7 percent. The authors characterized this overall prevalence as low. All 85 women with positive results had a retrievable genotype result. Within this positive group, 78 women, or 91.8 percent, carried at least one high-risk genotype as designated by the assay manufacturer. Furthermore, 66 of the HPV-positive women, corresponding to 77.6 percent, carried a carcinogenic genotype classified under Group 1 by the International Agency for Research on Cancer. In the genotype-specific analysis, HPV52 and HPV58 were the most frequently detected viral strains in the community sample. HPV52 was detected in 20 of the 85 HPV-positive women (23.5 percent), while HPV58 was identified in 14 women (16.5 percent). These were followed by HPV16, HPV51, and HPV59, each detected in 10 of the 85 positive women, representing 11.8 percent for each respective type. Genotype HPV18 was detected in 4 women, accounting for 4.7 percent. In keeping with the study’s protocol, genotype frequencies were not compared statistically. Additionally, multiple genotypes were detected in 25 of the 85 HPV-positive women, establishing an infection multiplicity of 29.4 percent. The study observed notable findings regarding carcinogenic types and vaccine-targeted genotypes. Among the 66 women confirmed to carry an IARC Group 1 carcinogenic genotype, 52 women, or 78.8 percent, carried neither HPV16 nor HPV18, meaning that nearly four in five women with an IARC Group 1 infection had types other than HPV16 or HPV18. When evaluating detection against current immunization targets, at least one genotype included in the nonavalent HPV vaccine was detected in 50 of the 85 HPV-positive women, corresponding to 58.8 percent of those infected. Researchers Cynthia Sifenjane Phiri and Pizga Kumwenda reviewed clinical records from May 2021 to December 2022 to examine viral distribution among local patients. The investigation evaluated how viral presence intersected with demographic factors and health indicators in Mzuzu City, identifying a substantial burden of high-risk infections within the urban clinical cohort. Human papillomavirus infection is the primary cause of cervical cancer, which remains a major public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in Malawi. Because cervical malignancies present severe risks to women across the country, establishing the local distribution of circulating viral types and associated risk factors is essential for optimising screening and vaccination strategies. The study evaluated these clinical dynamics by examining the specific type categories circulating among women seeking gynecological care in Mzuzu. The research team conducted a retrospective cross-sectional review involving 385 women who accessed gynecological care at Mzuzu Urban Health Centre over the twenty-month study timeframe. The investigators reviewed patient clinical records to gather data on age, residential location, and human immunodeficiency virus status alongside diagnostic laboratory results. By compiling these standardized clinical variables across the patient sample, the authors utilized descriptive statistics to assess the overall prevalence of high-risk viral infection and determine genotype patterns. Discover more Buy Maps Book Local Tours Check Symptoms Book a Checkup infections Viral DNA detection and genotyping were performed using the Xpert HPV assay. This diagnostic system identifies HPV 16 and HPV 18/45 individually while detecting a pooled group of eleven other high-risk genotypes. Utilizing this molecular testing platform allowed the researchers to detect critical oncogenic strains while tracking the broader distribution of high-risk infections that fall into the pooled category under the assay protocol. Genotype results showed that the pooled group of eleven other high-risk types predominated, appearing in 34 percent of screened women. In comparison, HPV 18/45 was detected in 11.7 percent of the cohort, while HPV 16 was identified in 9.1 percent. Multiple concurrent infections were documented in 26.7 percent of positive cases, with the most common combination consisting of HPV 18/45 alongside the pooled group of other high-risk types. The study observed notable differences in infection rates across age groups and residential locations. The highest infection rate occurred among women younger than 26 years, reaching 55.6 percent. Geographically, Mzuzu South recorded the largest share of viral cases, accounting for 49.2 percent of all positive results. These findings highlighted a high viral frequency among younger women and a substantial concentration in specific urban residential areas. Viral presence was also notably higher among women living with human immunodeficiency virus. High-risk human papillomavirus occurred in 51.6 percent of HIV-positive participants compared to 40 percent among HIV-negative women. This distribution demonstrated a clear clinical association between HIV status and high-risk viral detection within the outpatient population, emphasizing the heightened vulnerability observed among immunocompromised individuals attending the healthcare facility. Discover more infection Study Biology Explore History Support Causes Get Health Tips The authors concluded that women in Mzuzu City experience a high prevalence and diversity of high-risk viral categories, with non-vaccine types predominating alongside a notable HIV association. The findings emphasize the need for sustained molecular surveillance and consideration of broader-spectrum vaccines. Integrating screening into HIV care and prioritizing interventions for younger women may substantially reduce Malawi’s cervical cancer burden. Researchers sought to clarify the inconsistent associations previously reported in global literature regarding HPV involvement in these conditions, particularly given the varying prevalence rates observed across diverse geographic regions. The investigation included a cohort of 113 participants, categorized into three distinct groups: 42 patients with OLP, 31 patients with OSCC, and 40 healthy control subjects who displayed normal oral mucosa. This comparative structure allowed the research team to evaluate how the presence of specific viral genotypes correlated with different pathological states of the oral tissue. To determine the presence and identity of viral DNA within the oral environment, the researchers performed meticulous collection of epithelial cells from the respective lesions and healthy mucosa. The detection and genotyping process utilized a nested polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay, a technique chosen for its high sensitivity in identifying low levels of viral genetic material. The analysis classified the detected human papillomavirus genotypes into three primary categories: HPV16, HPV18, and a broader group encompassing other high-risk and low-risk genotypes, referred to as non-HPV16/18 types. This methodological approach enabled a granular view of the viral landscape present in the oral cavity of the study participants, providing a foundation for statistical analysis. The study results revealed varying degrees of HPV DNA detection across the examined groups. Any form of HPV DNA was identified in 25.0% of the healthy control group, 4.8% of the OLP group, and 29.0% of the OSCC group. When focusing specifically on the high-risk HPV16/18 genotypes, the researchers observed prevalence rates of 0% in healthy controls, 2.4% in the OLP group, and 12.9% in the OSCC group. Notably, the presence of HPV16 was detected exclusively within the cohort of patients diagnosed with oral squamous cell carcinoma, suggesting a specific, albeit limited, link between this high-risk strain and malignant oral disease within this particular study population. Discover more Book a Checkup View Census Data Get Health Tips Read Med Journals Find Cancer Care Statistical comparison between the OSCC group and the healthy control group indicated no statistically significant difference in the overall prevalence of any HPV DNA, with an odds ratio of 1.23 and a 95% confidence interval ranging from 0.43 to 3.53. This finding suggests that, in this specific population, the mere presence of any HPV DNA was not a standalone marker for increased risk of squamous cell carcinoma. However, when the analysis was restricted to the high-risk HPV16/18 genotypes, the researchers observed a significantly higher prevalence in the OSCC group compared to the healthy controls, with a p-value of 0.032 for the difference between the 4 out of 31 positive OSCC cases and 0 out of 40 positive healthy controls. The findings regarding the oral lichen planus group presented a distinct contrast. Patients with OLP demonstrated a significantly lower prevalence of any HPV DNA compared to the healthy control group, with an odds ratio of 0.15 and a p-value of 0.012. Furthermore, when compared directly to the OSCC group, the OLP participants showed a significantly lower likelihood of carrying HPV DNA, evidenced by an odds ratio of 8.18 and a p-value of 0.007. These observations highlight the complex and potentially protective or exclusionary interactions that may exist between the oral environment in OLP and the persistence or detection of HPV DNA. To ensure the robustness of these findings, the research team conducted logistic regression analyses, which were adjusted for the variables of age and sex. These adjustments were intended to isolate the relationship between HPV positivity and the different clinical groups from potential confounding factors associated with demographics. The resulting adjusted models indicated that neither age nor sex maintained a statistically significant association with HPV positivity in this study, reinforcing that the observed differences in viral prevalence were primarily driven by the underlying clinical condition of the oral mucosa rather than the demographic characteristics of the participants. Despite the detailed genotyping and statistical comparisons, the researchers acknowledged specific limitations inherent in their investigation. The most prominent constraint was the relatively small sample size, which limits the breadth of interpretation and the ability to extrapolate these findings to broader populations. Consequently, while the study provides important data regarding the prevalence of high-risk HPV genotypes in a Thai cohort, the authors emphasized the need for caution in interpreting these results and suggested that larger, multi-center studies may be necessary to further elucidate the relationship between HPV, oral lichen planus, and oral squamous cell carcinoma. Discover more Book a Dentist oral cancer Oral Cancer cancer Cancer In summary, the study demonstrates that HPV DNA is detectable in normal oral mucosa, oral lichen planus, and oral squamous cell carcinoma, with distinct patterns of prevalence. While high-risk HPV16/18 DNA was identified in a minority of the OSCC cases, its total absence in the healthy oral mucosa of this cohort suggests a potential area for further clinical investigation. The lack of evidence for increased HPV16/18 prevalence in OLP patients serves as a crucial data point for understanding oral potentially malignant disorders in this population, even as the researchers underscore the necessity for future research with larger sample sizes to validate and expand upon these findings.
