The research, carried out at a tertiary university hospital located in the Marmara region, evaluated three hundred women aged eighteen to forty-nine who presented for routine gynecological examinations. Although human papillomavirus represents one of the primary preventable contributors to cervical malignancy globally, only twelve point three percent of the surveyed cohort reported having received prior vaccination against the pathogen. Furthermore, participants achieved an average score of just eleven out of thirty-three on a standardized knowledge scale, underscoring substantial informational gaps among adult women actively accessing reproductive healthcare services within a regional medical center. Human papillomavirus constitutes one of the most widespread sexually transmitted infections across the globe and remains an established causative agent in cervical carcinoma as well as several other anogenital and oropharyngeal malignancies. Oncogenic risk is concentrated among twelve specific genotypes, with types sixteen and eighteen responsible for approximately seventy to eighty percent of cervical cancer cases documented internationally. Global estimates from 2020 identified cervical cancer as the fourth most frequently diagnosed female malignancy, accounting for more than six hundred four thousand newly diagnosed cases and approximately three hundred forty-one thousand related deaths annually. While international infection prevalence spans from two to forty-four percent, epidemiological data within Türkiye remain somewhat fragmented because the infection is not classified as a mandatory notifiable disease, yielding documented regional prevalence estimates between two point one and twenty-five point seven percent across various published cohorts. Primary prevention of these malignancies relies heavily on prophylactic immunization paired with safe sexual practices, providing the greatest clinical benefit when administered prior to sexual debut. Although global coverage for the initial vaccine dose among young adolescent girls rose from twenty percent in 2022 to twenty-seven percent in 2023, public health progress remains unevenly distributed across different healthcare systems and socioeconomic environments. Preventive health behaviors are frequently conceptualized through the Health Belief Model, which postulates that personal preventive actions depend on how individuals perceive their personal disease susceptibility, the severity of potential health consequences, and the balance between perceived practical barriers and therapeutic benefits. Within the domain of human papillomavirus prevention, general awareness and emotional concern can motivate health-seeking behavior, but excessive anxiety or unresolved safety misconceptions may paradoxically foster avoidance, highlighting the necessity of concurrently assessing factual knowledge, emotional concerns, and vaccination attitudes. Discover more Book a Checkup Check Symptoms Infectious infections infection To investigate these interlocking psychosocial determinants, researchers consecutively enrolled eligible women presenting for outpatient gynecological consultations between September and December 2025. Following the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology reporting guidelines, the investigators established an a priori statistical power calculation using specialized software, determining that a sample size of three hundred participants would provide eighty percent power to detect a medium multivariate effect size at a significance threshold of zero point zero five. Clinic staff approached three hundred thirty-five women, excluding seventeen individuals who failed to meet predefined clinical criteria and recording eighteen declines among three hundred eighteen invited candidates, which yielded an overall participation rate of ninety-four point three percent. Women diagnosed with current or past gynecological malignancies, active virus follow-up, cognitive impairments, or active psychiatric conditions were systematically excluded to maintain an analytically uniform sample of routine clinic attendees. Data collection occurred through standardized face-to-face interviews administered in private clinical consultation rooms, requiring approximately fifteen to twenty minutes per participant to complete four distinct instruments. Sociodemographic attributes, chronic disease history, and previous immunization status were captured using a seven-item descriptive questionnaire developed from relevant clinical literature, though detailed historical records concerning past screening smears or prior diagnostic viral testing were deliberately omitted from this instrument. Factual comprehension was measured using the thirty-three-item Turkish adaptation of the Human Papillomavirus Knowledge Scale, which exhibited strong internal consistency with a Cronbach’s alpha of zero point eighty-seven. Emotional and cognitive dimensions were evaluated through the nineteen-item Human Papilloma Virus Awareness and Concern Scale, which demonstrated an alpha coefficient of zero point eighty-three across three subscales, while vaccine-specific perceptions were quantified via the sixteen-item Carolina HPV Vaccination Attitudes and Beliefs Scale, similarly displaying an internal consistency of zero point eighty-three. Discover more Study Biology Infection hospital The enrolled cohort had an average age of thirty-four point fifty-five years, with approximately seventy-two point two percent reporting completion of at least a high school education, seventy-two point nine percent indicating married status, and seventy-four point eight percent describing their personal financial status as moderate. Across the total study sample, participants obtained a mean score of eleven point zero one on the thirty-three-item knowledge scale, reflecting widespread unfamiliarity with basic transmission dynamics, oncogenic potential, and preventive screening procedures. Conversely, participants recorded a mean awareness and concern score of forty-three point fifty-seven out of a theoretical maximum of seventy-six, alongside an average Carolina vaccination attitudes score of thirty-seven point eighteen. These baseline metrics revealed that while women presenting for gynecological care maintained moderate overall awareness and generally neutral-to-positive vaccine orientations, their actual baseline factual knowledge regarding the virus remained strikingly deficient. Unadjusted comparative analyses revealed that educational background was strongly associated with factual comprehension but showed no meaningful association with broader emotional or attitudinal scale metrics. Women who had completed high school education or beyond achieved significantly higher mean knowledge scores than participants who attained only primary school education, recording twelve point sixty-seven points compared to eight point seventy-nine points, a difference that reached statistical significance with a p-value below zero point zero zero one. However, awareness and concern scores did not differ significantly between primary and higher education groups, registering forty-three point zero seven and forty-three point seventy-five respectively. Similarly, attitudes toward vaccination showed no statistically significant disparity across educational tiers. Comparisons based on vaccination status demonstrated that previously vaccinated individuals possessed substantially higher knowledge scores than unvaccinated peers, averaging fifteen point ninety-one against ten point sixty-three, while awareness and attitude scores remained statistically indistinguishable between vaccinated and unvaccinated groups. Multivariate analysis of variance was subsequently performed to evaluate how categorical demographic factors related to the combined profile of knowledge, awareness, and vaccination beliefs across participants. Preliminary data diagnostics confirmed multivariate normality, linear relationships among dependent outcomes, an absence of disruptive multicollinearity, and homogeneity of variance-covariance matrices verified through Box’s test. The multivariate model demonstrated a statistically significant association between educational attainment and the composite dependent measure, generating an F-statistic of two point seventy-six with three and two hundred ninety-three degrees of freedom, an associated p-value of zero point zero forty-four, and a partial eta-squared of zero point zero five. A parallel multivariate evaluation established that marital status was likewise significantly associated with the combined outcome vector, yielding an F-statistic of two point sixty-four, a p-value of zero point zero forty-one, and an identical partial eta-squared of zero point zero five, indicating modest overall effect sizes. Bivariate correlational assessments highlighted complex and divergent relationships among the three primary psychosocial constructs evaluated in the patient cohort. Total knowledge scores exhibited a robust positive linear correlation with human papillomavirus awareness and concern, demonstrated by a Pearson correlation coefficient of zero point sixty with a ninety-five percent confidence interval extending from zero point fifty-two to zero point sixty-seven. Awareness and concern also correlated positively and strongly with Carolina vaccine beliefs, yielding a coefficient of zero point sixty-one with a confidence interval between zero point fifty-three and zero point sixty-eight. In striking contrast, factual knowledge displayed a weak but statistically significant inverse correlation with vaccination beliefs, characterized by a coefficient of negative zero point sixteen with a confidence interval spanning negative zero point twenty-seven to negative zero point zero five and a p-value of zero point zero zero five. The researchers emphasized that this weak negative association warrants careful interpretation rather than an assumption that elevated knowledge degrades vaccine receptivity. Because the Carolina scale incorporates perceived harms, practical barriers, and medical uncertainty rather than straightforward factual approval, individuals possessing greater knowledge may simply exhibit heightened sensitivity to procedural costs, access hurdles, or public health debates. This observation aligns with broader evidence indicating that health information alone cannot reliably drive preventive health practices without concurrent structural support. In Türkiye, where the human papillomavirus vaccine has not been incorporated into the routine National Immunization Program, individuals must secure doses through direct out-of-pocket expenditure. Several essential methodological limitations constrain the generalizability of these findings beyond the specific tertiary clinical setting examined by the study authors. The cross-sectional design inherently precludes establishing causal directions among educational background, knowledge gains, and health behaviors, while recruiting exclusively from a single academic medical center in the Marmara region introduces potential selection bias toward individuals with comparatively higher healthcare-seeking tendencies. Additionally, unmeasured clinical variables—such as individual Pap smear histories, previous viral testing, reproductive parity, and specific physician recommendations—precluded the construction of fully adjusted multivariable regression models, leaving open the likelihood of residual confounding. Because statistical comparisons were interpreted at nominal significance levels without formal family-wise error adjustments, significant correlations should be viewed as exploratory. The authors concluded that routine gynecological appointments provide an invaluable clinical window for structured, evidence-based counseling to bridge the gap between abstract awareness and actual cancer prevention. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 21, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer Portable Test Detects High-Risk Papillomavirus Messenger RNA in Mozambique Pilot Study by November 20, 2026 in Cancer Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Portable Test Detects High-Risk Papillomavirus Messenger RNA in Mozambique Pilot Study Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A portable molecular assay capable of detecting high-risk human papillomavirus messenger RNA directly in resource-limited clinical environments has demonstrated feasibility in an initial clinical pilot conducted at Maputo Central Hospital in Mozambique. Cervical cancer represents the most prevalent malignancy among women in Mozambique, where structural limitations in routine screening infrastructure contribute substantially to a high clinical disease burden. While the World Health Organization recommends screening via high-risk human papillomavirus deoxyribonucleic acid testing, positive DNA findings often reflect transient infections that clear without therapeutic intervention. Because viral DNA testing possesses limited specificity for high-grade cervical precancer, routine screen-and-treat strategies frequently precipitate significant overtreatment, placing severe logistical and financial demands on public healthcare systems. To evaluate potential alternatives capable of distinguishing clinically consequential infections from benign viral carriage, researchers deployed an accessible isothermal platform designed to amplify viral messenger RNA. Overexpression of viral E6 and E7 messenger RNA occurs when high-risk viral sequences integrate into host cellular genomes, establishing this transcript as a considerably more specific biomarker for high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. Standard commercial platforms that quantify messenger RNA have historically required centralized laboratory facilities, specialized power sources, and complex technical extraction protocols, precluding point-of-care deployment in low- and middle-income countries. The investigational pilot sought to evaluate whether reverse transcription recombinase polymerase amplification performed on a battery-compatible portable fluorimeter could deliver accurate on-site molecular evaluations from provider-collected cervical specimens. The clinical evaluation enrolled twenty-two consecutive non-pregnant female participants presenting with an intact cervix who had previously screened positive via visual inspection with acetic acid at community clinics in Mozambique. Because visual inspection with acetic acid serves as a routine frontline triage tool, these participants represented an elevated-risk referral cohort rather than an unselected general screening demographic. Within this cohort, sixteen participants were confirmed to be individuals living with human immunodeficiency virus, representing a key focus group given that viral coinfection accelerates progression toward invasive cervical malignancies. Experienced clinical personnel obtained cervicovaginal specimens using standardized cytobrushes agitated within preservation medium, alongside diagnostic colposcopic examinations that supplied targeted or junctional tissue biopsies for definitive histopathological confirmation. Processing specimens in an environment lacking high-speed programmable centrifugation necessitated substantial modifications to standard nucleic acid extraction protocols. Laboratory personnel adapted commercial spin-column isolation kits to operate using an electric benchtop quick spinner, systematically doubling routine liquid spinning intervals from one minute to two minutes while extending final elution periods to three minutes. Extracted eluates underwent enzymatic digestion with deoxyribonuclease at thirty-seven degrees Celsius for thirty minutes to eliminate residual host and viral DNA, followed by heat denaturation at seventy-five degrees Celsius. This complete field-adapted sample preparation routine achieved total extraction times of approximately seventy-five minutes across hands-on manipulations and modest incubation stages without relying on refrigerated high-speed benchtop microcentrifuges. Purified RNA samples underwent isothermal reverse transcription recombinase polymerase amplification targeting the oncogenic genotypes HPV 16, HPV 18, and HPV 45, supplemented by an internal beta-actin cellular adequacy control. Amplification and real-time optical tracking were executed on an Axxin T8-ISO fluorimeter, completing qualitative signal detection within fifteen minutes of machine run time. For analytical validation, identical RNA extracts were simultaneously assayed via gold-standard portable reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction on a specialized mini thermocycler. To mirror clinical standards, independent aliquots were evaluated for high-risk viral DNA using the commercial Xpert HPV platform, while blinded consensus histopathology from at least two local pathologists served as the absolute diagnostic arbiter. Analytical comparisons between the portable isothermal platform and the reference quantitative PCR instrument revealed complete diagnostic concordance, demonstrating one hundred percent agreement across all twenty-two patient specimens. The molecular assays identified four samples positive for HPV 16 messenger RNA and one sample positive for HPV 18 messenger RNA, while seventeen specimens tested negative for the three targeted genotypes alongside positive amplification of the cellular control. No specimens tested positive for HPV 45 transcripts by either analytical method. Beyond absolute concordance in diagnostic classification, the isothermal technique substantially accelerated laboratory workflows, requiring approximately one and a half hours for total sample-to-answer processing compared to three and three-quarter hours required by the portable quantitative PCR baseline. Evaluation against verified tissue histopathology highlighted notable differences between messenger RNA detection and commercial DNA testing regarding clinical lesion classification. Ten study participants exhibited verified high-grade disease classified as cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or higher, including individual cases of confirmed squamous cell carcinoma and cervical adenocarcinoma. The reverse transcription recombinase polymerase amplification test accurately identified five high-grade lesions without generating false-positive determinations among benign biopsies, yielding a positive predictive value of one hundred percent and a negative predictive value of seventy-one percent. Conversely, the commercial DNA platform correctly identified eight high-grade lesions but registered three positive results in benign tissues, producing a positive predictive value of seventy-three percent and a negative predictive value of eighty-two percent. Analysis of diagnostic discrepancies revealed that two high-grade lesions missed by the isothermal messenger RNA test harbored oncogenic viral genotypes distinct from types 16, 18, or 45, as confirmed by extended genotyping on the DNA panel. When researchers excluded these discordant cases involving viral genotypes intentionally omitted from the initial assay design, the negative predictive value of the isothermal platform rose to seventy-seven percent. Because existing commercial DNA assays routinely screen for fourteen high-risk viral genotypes, the narrower three-genotype coverage of the prototype transcript test inherently constrained its negative predictive capacity. Nevertheless, the total absence of false-positive detections highlights the potential utility of messenger RNA quantification to prevent unnecessary surgical excisions or ablative interventions in primary care clinics. Despite promising operational metrics, investigators documented significant technical and logistical barriers that currently preclude routine autonomous implementation in low-resource clinics. Reagents for both amplification assays required continuous cold-chain maintenance, traveling from Houston to Maputo packed in specialized vacuum flasks with ice packs before transfer into local freezers. Furthermore, while the portable fluorimeter executed amplification rapidly, the seventy-five-minute extraction protocol involved numerous delicate pipetting steps executed by highly trained personnel, which remains impractical for busy community clinics lacking advanced laboratory infrastructure. The modest pilot sample size also prevented formal statistical calculations of clinical sensitivity and specificity, underscoring that observed predictive values reflect an enriched referral cohort rather than broad population screening. Future development efforts must incorporate additional high-risk viral genotypes—notably types 31, 33, 35, 52, and 58—to match the comprehensive diagnostic coverage required for clinical deployment across Sub-Saharan Africa. Transitioning the platform to lyophilized, temperature-stable reagent formulations and establishing streamlined, extraction-free lysis methods will also be essential to eliminate multi-step centrifugation. While expanded clinical trials in larger cohorts of women living with HIV remain necessary to establish definitive sensitivity thresholds, this pilot demonstrates that rapid, isothermal messenger RNA diagnostics can be successfully conducted on-site in low-income healthcare settings. The imperative for accessible cervical screening alternatives is particularly acute in Mozambique, where disease patterns intersect with severe structural healthcare challenges. The high cervical cancer burden across the country stems largely from insufficient human papillomavirus vaccination coverage coupled with a lack of adequate screening and treatment facilities. This clinical burden is further amplified by widespread transmission of the human immunodeficiency virus, which serves as a recognized risk factor for cervical malignancies. While the World Health Organization recommends screening through high-risk viral DNA detection, the commercial nucleic acid amplification tests identified in global health surveys remain largely inaccessible or impractical for routine primary care deployment in resource-constrained lower-income settings. Understanding of human papillomavirus molecular biology explains why targeting viral transcripts offers clinical advantages over DNA detection. In typical transient infections, viral genomes remain episomal and frequently resolve without malignant transformation. When high-risk human papillomavirus DNA integrates into human host cellular genomes, overexpression of oncogenic E6 and E7 viral messenger RNA occurs, substantially elevating the likelihood of high-grade precancerous lesions. Prior systematic reviews and clinical evaluations have indicated that messenger RNA testing yields a higher positive predictive value of seventy-eight percent for high-grade cervical precancer compared to fifteen to twenty-five percent for DNA assays, even though both approaches maintain high negative predictive values around ninety-nine percent. Nevertheless, commercial transcript assays such as the Aptima platform have historically remained restricted to centralized reference laboratories in low- and middle-income regions. Operational evaluations highlighted further analytical nuances regarding platform performance and field laboratory requirements. Reaction outputs on the portable fluorimeter were analyzed utilizing custom software scripts with baseline subtraction, although the instrument can directly display real-time fluorescence curves and deliver autonomous categorical classifications without external computing hardware. While beta-actin transcript amplification verified sufficient cellular content across all runs, the mobile laboratory lacked benchtop spectrophotometers, bioanalyzers, or gel electrophoresis equipment to determine formal RNA integrity numbers. Furthermore, global health recommendations established by the World Health Organization suggest five-year rescreening intervals for viral messenger RNA testing due to limited longitudinal performance evidence, contrasting with ten-year intervals for DNA-based protocols, while currently withholding generalized testing recommendations for women living with human immunodeficiency virus until broader clinical trials define diagnostic thresholds. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 21, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer Six-Year Uganda Study Shows High-Risk Non-16/18 HPV Genotypes Dominate Regional Testing by November 20, 2026 in Cancer Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Six-Year Uganda Study Shows High-Risk Non-16/18 HPV Genotypes Dominate Regional Testing Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A six-year retrospective review of laboratory records at Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital in southwestern Uganda has identified an overall high-risk human papillomavirus prevalence of 28.52 percent among tested individuals. Analyzing 4,852 test results compiled between January 2020 and July 2025, investigators observed a gradual upward trend in positive diagnoses across the observation window. The clinical significance of monitoring high-risk viral strains stems directly from their role in disease progression, as persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus causes almost all cervical cancer cases. With global healthcare frameworks steadily moving towards primary testing for cervical cancer screening, understanding regional genotype dynamics has become increasingly important. In this retrospective study, the research team reviewed laboratory records from the regional facility covering a six-year period from January 2020 through July 2025. The investigative protocol gathered detailed data on participant age, district of residence, HIV status, individual test outcomes, detected viral genotypes, and exact dates of testing. All extracted clinical records and multi-year diagnostic datasets were compiled, structured, and statistically analyzed using STATA version 17 software. Analysis of the 4,852 retrieved test records established that diagnostic positivity varied substantially across participant demographics, displaying an inverse relationship with age. The prevalence of high-risk human papillomavirus was highest among the youngest participants aged under 19 years, reaching 66.71 percent based on 12 positive results from 18 tests. Across older cohorts, the measured prevalence of high-risk infections demonstrated a steady and continuous decrease with increasing participant age. Beyond overall positivity, the distribution of identified viral strains revealed that more than half of all positive tests belonged to non-traditional high-risk classifications. Specifically, 65.12 percent of positive results, representing 898 of the 1,379 positive cases, involved non-16/18/45 high-risk genotypes categorized by the investigators as other high-risk HPV. This genotype category also demonstrated a persistent rise over time, climbing from 61.04 percent in 2020 to 63.53 percent in 2025, while also exhibiting a gradual decline with increasing participant age. When examining specific clinical subpopulations, the research team found that participants living with HIV consistently exhibited high rates of these non-16/18/45 genotypes. Within the HIV-positive population evaluated at the referral center, the prevalence of the other high-risk HPV genotype group remained persistently elevated across testing intervals, recording 64.79 percent from 46 of 71 cases in 2020, 66.55 percent from 189 of 284 cases in 2023, and 63.53 percent from 54 of 85 cases in 2025. In their conclusion, the authors noted an elevated overall prevalence of high-risk infections, driven especially by genotypes categorized as other high-risk HPV that inversely correlate with participant age. Based on these observed distributions, the team emphasized the need for implementation of extended high-risk HPV genotyping protocols in regional diagnostic settings. The researchers also highlighted the necessity for further prospective studies to more fully describe individual genotype prevalence, geographic distribution, and longitudinal epidemiological trends. supplementary_news.content: 18岁女孩检出18种HPV亚型阳性,包含10种高危型;医生:极其少见,远期癌变风险显著升高 华医网 2026-11-16 05:38发布于北京 问AI · 年轻未生育女性多重感染如何护生育功能? 导 语 什么情况下HPV病毒会导致癌变? 近日,杭州市临平区妇幼保健院妇科接诊了一例极其少见的HPV多重感染病例:年仅18岁的玲玲因外阴持续性疼痛半月余前来就诊,最终确诊为外阴尖锐湿疣,且一次性检出18种HPV亚型阳性,其中高危型多达10种,属于临床极少见的多重混合感染。 玲玲的HPV检验报告/医院供图 接诊医生介绍,玲玲来杭探亲,半个月来外阴隐隐疼痛,总觉得有异物感,最近难受得越来越厉害,正常生活都受影响。专科查体发现其外阴长了典型的菜花状赘生物,从外观来看很像尖锐湿疣。为了查清到底感染了哪些病毒,医生给她做了高精度HPV分型检测,结果让人意外:一共查出18种HPV亚型同时阳性,感染的亚型多、病毒载量很高。 值得高度警惕的是,在18种阳性亚型中,包含10种高危致癌型HPV,是诱发宫颈上皮内病变甚至进展为宫颈癌的核心风险亚型。一次性多重混合感染18种亚型且高危占比极高,提示患者病毒暴露时间长、感染复杂、远期癌变风险显著升高。接诊医生结合玲玲的症状、专科体征及精准HPV分型结果,最终确诊为外阴尖锐湿疣、HPV多重高危感染,目前正在积极治疗中。 医生提醒,尖锐湿疣由人乳头瘤病毒感染所致,多表现为生殖器部位菜花状赘生物,可伴随疼痛、异物感。该患者同时合并多亚型HPV混合感染,尤其是多种高危型持续感染,远期存在宫颈病变风险,需规范治疗并长期随访复查。 那么,如果年轻未生育的女性感染了HPV该怎么办呢?医生介绍:重点要分层评估、避免过度治疗,保护生育功能。大多数生殖道HPV感染依靠自身免疫力,1~2年内自行清除病毒,属于一过性感染,不等于宫颈癌。高危型HPV持续感染才会导致宫颈癌前病变或宫颈癌的发生;单纯HPV阳性、TCT正常≠癌前病变。一般年轻女性HPV感染率高,但病毒清除能力强,所以不要过度恐慌。 建议提高自身免疫力,这对于清除病毒最关键,规律睡眠、减重、均衡饮食,戒烟(吸烟显著降低清除率,增加病变进展风险);适度运动,避免长期熬夜、巨大精神压力等。此外,性生活时建议全程佩戴避孕套,减少交叉反复感染。 如何判断自己是否感染了HPV? 1. 根据症状判断 如果您的皮肤表面出现了不明疣体,有或痛或痒的感觉;或出现非经期出血、同房后出血、白带异常(量多、色黄、有异味)等症状时,建议第一时间到医院做个HPV检查。 2. 无症状时 坚持定期体检,通过HPV联合TCT筛查,可以判断有无HPV感染及宫颈病变。 一项基于美国人群的研究显示,有性行为的男性和女性一生中感染HPV的几率高达80%~90%,而因此患上宫颈癌的女性仅占极小的比例。 人体在感染HPV之后,大多可以通过自身的免疫机制将其清除,所以多数HPV感染是一过性且没有临床症状的,不会产生病变。 什么情况下HPV病毒会导致癌变? 1. HPV病毒持续感染 事实上,导致宫颈癌的主要原因不是感染了HPV,而是无法将其从体内及时清除,使得感染进入了持续阶段。换句话说,HPV持续感染才是宫颈病变发展为宫颈癌的必要条件,而单纯的HPV感染不一定会导致宫颈癌。 从HPV感染发展为宫颈浸润癌可能需要10年、15年甚至20年的时间,经过“HPV感染→持续性HPV感染引起宫颈上皮细胞病变→持续性HPV感染引起宫颈癌前病变→宫颈浸润癌”的四步曲,最终进展为恶性肿瘤。 2. 高危型HPV病毒 是否导致癌变也与感染的HPV型别有关。目前已经发现的HPV有200多种,其中约40种可感染生殖道,根据致癌性的不同分为高危型和低危型。高危型HPV主要有12种,引起宫颈癌前病变II级及以上的几率超过90%,存在致癌风险;低危型HPV主要有11种,主要导致湿疣类病变和宫颈上皮增生,引发宫颈癌的几率不到5%。 从目前的研究数据看,宫颈癌多见于40岁以上女性,从高危型HPV持续感染到宫颈癌前病变,再到发展为宫颈浸润癌,至少需要10~15 年的时间,但约25%的患者会在5年内发展为浸润癌。 日常生活中如何预防HPV病毒感染? HPV虽然主要通过性行为传播,但也可能通过毛巾、便盆、母婴等途径间接传播。预防HPV感染和干预HPV感染后的疾病进程,是HPV感染防治的关键。只有正确认识,规范治疗,才能避免不必要的损伤。 1. 注射HPV疫苗 九价HPV疫苗的预防效果优于四价和二价。目前国内九价HPV疫苗由16~26岁扩龄至9~45岁。在综合考虑价格的前提下,推荐根据适合的年龄段进行选择。 HPV疫苗可以从根本上阻断HPV传播,是特异、有效的预防措施,但对于正在感染相应HPV型别的人群不具有保护作用,因此推荐在高危型HPV感染之前进行接种。 2. 注意私处卫生 养成每天温水清洁阴部的习惯,少穿紧身、不透气的衣物,不给HPV创造藏身之处;性生活前后,男女双方都要用温水清洁外阴部,减少将HPV带入宫颈的机会;同时警惕间接传播方式,如不干净的马桶、宾馆的床单、毛巾等,病毒可以通过皮肤接触,在个人免疫力薄弱时感染。 3. 定期筛查 推荐联合筛查,即在进行HPV病毒筛查的同时,进行宫颈液基薄层细胞学检测(TCT)。如TCT发现异常,推荐进一步阴道镜检查,通过细胞活检取得病理学证据。如阴道镜检查无异常,考虑为慢性宫颈炎。如阴道镜发现异常,可能存在宫颈上皮内瘤变,分为低级别病变和高级别病变。 成年女性建议每2~3年进行一次HPV或TCT筛查,如果是联合筛查,可以间隔3~5年复查一次。 由于HPV疫苗目前尚不能预防所有的高危型HPV病毒,建议有性生活的女性,无论是否接种过疫苗,都应定期进行宫颈癌筛查。 来 源 / 潮新闻、福建省二院健康管理中心

supplementary_news.content_title: How Mexican Scientist Eva Ramón Gallegos Eliminated HPV in 29 Women
supplementary_news.content: Eliminating a persistent oncogenic viral infection without cutting, burning, or scarring delicate reproductive tissue represents one of modern gynecological bioengineering’s most sought-after milestones. At Mexico’s National Polytechnic Institute, biomedical scientist Dr. Eva Ramón Gallegos spent twenty years refining a non-invasive photodynamic therapy that destroys Human Papillomavirus at the cellular level while sparing healthy tissue. In a landmark Mexico City clinical cohort, her light-activated protocol achieved complete molecular eradication of HPV in one hundred percent of twenty-nine women carrying the virus without premalignant cervical lesions, while clearing infections in nearly two-thirds of patients with precancerous changes. Building on earlier clinical phases across Oaxaca and Veracruz involving more than four hundred women, her work shows how prodrug biochemistry and red-laser physics offer a painless, fertility-sparing defense against cervical cancer. Dr. Eva Ramón Gallegos spent twenty years developing non-invasive cervical photodynamic therapy. Twenty Years of Persistence at Mexico’s National Polytechnic Institute Research at ENCB-IPN in Mexico City translated photochemistry into public women’s healthcare. For decades, cervical cancer has ranked among the deadliest malignancies affecting women across Mexico and Latin America, disproportionately striking communities where routine screening arrives late. Even as national screening expanded, millions of women diagnosed with persistent high-risk Human Papillomavirus faced a difficult clinical gap between passive watchful waiting and invasive surgical excision. Working inside the National School of Biological Sciences at the National Polytechnic Institute—known as ENCB-IPN—Dr. Eva Ramón Gallegos set out two decades ago to close that divide using light-activated molecular medicine. Trained in cytopathology, biomedicine, and photodynamic oncology, she studied how photosensitive porphyrin precursors accumulate selectively inside metabolically altered tumor and viral host cells across breast, melanoma, and cervical tissues. Unlike chemotherapy or surgery, photodynamic therapy pairs an inert chemical precursor with harmless visible wavelengths so cellular destruction occurs exclusively where prodrug, light, and oxygen intersect. Sustaining a twenty-year translational program inside a public university demanded steady perseverance across cell-culture assays, optical dosimetry calibration, pathology validation, and multi-state patient follow-up. When IPN reported the Mexico City clinical outcomes in early 2019, the results resonated worldwide by uniting sensitive polymerase chain reaction verification with outpatient accessibility. How High-Risk HPV Oncogenes Drive Cervical Cancer Progression High-risk HPV capsids infect basal cervical keratinocytes and hijack cell-cycle checkpoints. Human Papillomavirus is a non-enveloped, icosahedral double-stranded DNA virus carrying roughly eight thousand base pairs inside a fifty-five-nanometer protein capsid. More than two hundred HPV genotypes exist, yet two high-risk mucosal strains—HPV-16 and HPV-18—cause approximately seventy percent of all invasive cervical carcinomas worldwide. Infection begins when viral particles slip through microscopic mucosal abrasions in the cervical transformation zone to enter dividing basal keratinocytes along the basement membrane. Although healthy immunity clears roughly eighty to ninety percent of transient exposures within two years, persistent high-risk infections unleash two viral oncoproteins—E6 and E7—that dismantle cellular anti-cancer defenses. Viral E6 recruits the host E6AP ubiquitin ligase complex to tag and degrade p53, the master guardian protein normally responsible for halting DNA-damaged cells or initiating apoptosis, while simultaneously activating telomerase reverse transcriptase to immortalize infected clones. Simultaneously, E7 binds and inactivates retinoblastoma protein pRb, releasing E2F transcription factors that force differentiating epithelial cells back into unchecked S-phase DNA replication and progressive chromosomal instability. Because HPV replicates strictly inside intraepithelial keratinocytes without causing viremia or lytic cell rupture, the virus hides subtly from systemic antibodies while gradually integrating its oncogenes into human chromosomes. Over years, persistent E6 and E7 expression drives cervical epithelium through cervical intraepithelial neoplasia stages CIN 1, CIN 2, and CIN 3 toward invasive squamous or glandular carcinoma. Topical 5-ALA and Selective Protoporphyrin IX Accumulation HPV-infected cells convert topical 5-ALA selectively into photoactive protoporphyrin IX. The biochemical cornerstone of Dr. Ramón Gallegos’s protocol is delta-aminolevulinic acid, or 5-ALA, a small naturally occurring amino-ketone that every human cell already uses to synthesize heme for cytochromes and hemoglobin. Rather than injecting systemic synthetic photosensitizers that leave patients sensitive to daylight for weeks, clinicians apply a gentle localized 5-ALA solution topically onto the ectocervix and endocervical canal. Because exogenous 5-ALA bypasses feedback inhibition at the first step of heme synthesis yet remains completely non-toxic in the dark, it diffuses safely across dysplastic and HPV-infected mucosa over a four-hour incubation window. Inside HPV-infected and dysplastic cells, warped Warburg-like metabolic enzyme ratios—elevated cytosolic porphobilinogen deaminase paired with sluggish mitochondrial ferrochelatase—stall final ferrous iron insertion into heme. Because that enzymatic bottleneck blocks heme completion, infected cells trap massive intracellular concentrations of the immediate fluorescent precursor: photoactive protoporphyrin IX, abbreviated PpIX. Healthy surrounding squamous cells and underlying stromal fibroblasts maintain balanced ferrochelatase kinetics, swiftly converting excess PpIX into harmless, non-photosensitive heme. Under diagnostic blue-violet illumination near four hundred five nanometers, PpIX-enriched viral patches emit unmistakable brick-red fluorescence, confirming millimeter-level biochemical selectivity before therapeutic laser exposure begins. 630–635 nm Red Laser Excitation and Singlet Oxygen Physics Non-thermal red laser light excites PpIX to generate short-lived cytotoxic singlet oxygen. Four hours after topical 5-ALA application, when the PpIX concentration ratio between infected keratinocytes and normal stroma peaks, clinicians illuminate the cervix with a calibrated non-thermal red laser tuned to 630 to 635 nanometers. Although PpIX absorbs violet wavelengths strongly at the surface, biophysicists deliberately target its red Q-band absorption peak because 630-to-635-nanometer photons avoid hemoglobin absorption and penetrate several millimeters deep into endocervical crypts where latent HPV resides. Absorbing red photons promotes PpIX into an excited singlet state that undergoes quantum intersystem crossing into a long-lived triplet state, transferring energy via Type II photochemistry directly to dissolved triplet oxygen to generate cytotoxic singlet oxygen (1O2). Because singlet oxygen survives less than a microsecond and diffuses fewer than one hundred nanometers—smaller than a single mitochondrion—oxidative destruction stays locked strictly inside PpIX-loaded HPV host cells through five synergistic mechanisms: Mitochondrial apoptosis induction: Singlet oxygen oxidizes inner mitochondrial lipids where PpIX forms, releasing cytochrome-c to guide HPV-infected keratinocytes into clean programmed apoptosis without inflammatory necrosis. Singlet oxygen oxidizes inner mitochondrial lipids where PpIX forms, releasing cytochrome-c to guide HPV-infected keratinocytes into clean programmed apoptosis without inflammatory necrosis. Direct viral DNA and oncoprotein oxidation: Reactive oxygen species cleave intracellular HPV episomes and denature E6 and E7 oncoproteins across basal epithelial layers. Reactive oxygen species cleave intracellular HPV episomes and denature E6 and E7 oncoproteins across basal epithelial layers. Deep endocervical crypt reach: Coherent 630–635 nm red photons penetrate glandular infoldings several millimeters deep where superficial cautery misses latent virus. Coherent 630–635 nm red photons penetrate glandular infoldings several millimeters deep where superficial cautery misses latent virus. Local dendritic T-cell priming: Apoptotic viral host cells expose viral capsid antigens and damage signals that recruit Langerhans cells and CD8-positive T lymphocytes against residual virus. Apoptotic viral host cells expose viral capsid antigens and damage signals that recruit Langerhans cells and CD8-positive T lymphocytes against residual virus. Concurrent co-pathogen clearance: Cervicovaginal bacteria and fungi rapidly accumulate porphyrins too, clearing co-infections that otherwise fuel chronic mucosal inflammation. Patients remain awake without anesthesia throughout the brief outpatient illumination, feeling at most gentle warmth while laser fluence stays below thermal thresholds. Preserving Cervical Anatomy Without Surgical Scarring Extracellular collagen matrix stays intact so cervical tissue regenerates without surgical scarring. Comparing photodynamic therapy against standard excisional procedures highlights why reproductive specialists and maternal-fetal medicine physicians welcomed ENCB-IPN’s results across Latin America. Conventional loop electrosurgical excision (LEEP) and cold-knife conization save lives whenever high-grade dysplasia nears micro-invasion, yet surgically cutting a wedge-shaped cone of fibromuscular stroma carries documented obstetric trade-offs for younger patients. Removing structural cervical collagen shortens functional cervical length and weakens sphincter integrity, measurably elevating future risks of cervical insufficiency, second-trimester miscarriage, premature membrane rupture, preterm delivery, and endocervical canal stenosis. Thermal cautery and liquid-nitrogen cryotherapy can also leave fibrotic scar tissue that pulls the squamocolumnar transformation zone inward, making subsequent colposcopic surveillance harder to interpret accurately. Post-treatment cytology and colposcopy confirmed healthy epithelial regeneration across treated cohorts. Photodynamic therapy avoids structural tissue loss altogether because acellular type-I and type-III collagen fibers and elastin networks neither synthesize protoporphyrin IX nor denature under non-thermal 630-nanometer illumination. Even microvascular basement membranes beneath the cervical epithelium recover smoothly after transient vasoconstriction, supplying oxygen and growth factors without triggering myofibroblast scar contraction. As apoptotic HPV-infected cells slough away cleanly over several days, intact collagen scaffolds guide healthy basal stem cells to resurface a smooth, unscarred cervix across five structured outpatient steps: Baseline multimodal diagnostic profiling: Every enrolled participant underwent Pap cytology, high-magnification colposcopy, targeted histopathology when lesions appeared, and baseline polymerase chain reaction genotyping to map exact high-risk HPV strains and co-infections. Localized topical 5-ALA prodrug application: Clinicians applied calibrated delta-aminolevulinic acid gel directly over the ectocervix and endocervical canal using a sterile cervical applicator without needles, local anesthetic injections, or surgical clamps. Four-hour selective metabolic conversion window: Patients rested comfortably for roughly four hours while metabolically altered HPV-infected and dysplastic cells converted 5-ALA selectively into brick-red fluorescent protoporphyrin IX. Scheduled 48-hour red-laser photodynamic sessions: Precision optical fiber delivery illuminated the cervical transformation zone and endocervical canal at 630–635 nm across scheduled outpatient visits spaced forty-eight hours apart. Longitudinal cytological and PCR verification: Follow-up evaluations months post-therapy repeated colposcopy, cytology, and sensitive viral DNA amplification to verify both histological tissue normalization and true molecular HPV clearance. Inside the Oaxaca, Veracruz, and Mexico City Clinical Cohorts Fluorescence spectroscopy guided optimal prodrug concentration and 48-hour laser dosing intervals. Rather than relying on a single small pilot group, Dr. Ramón Gallegos systematically refined optical dosimetry and prodrug kinetics across distinct geographic cohorts totaling four hundred forty-nine Mexican women. In the earlier clinical phase conducted across public clinics in Oaxaca and Veracruz, four hundred twenty women received three photodynamic sessions spaced forty-eight hours apart. That initial regimen achieved eighty-five percent complete HPV eradication among lesion-free HPV carriers, eighty-five percent clearance in women presenting with both HPV and premalignant lesions, and forty-two percent resolution in HPV-negative lesions. By tracking cervical surface porphyrin fluorescence before and after each illumination cycle, ENCB-IPN biophysicists discovered that doubling the topical 5-ALA concentration across two forty-eight-hour treatment schemes achieved deeper, more uniform PpIX saturation down to basal stem-cell layers. Painless outpatient delivery made advanced photodynamic care welcoming for Mexico City participants. Testing that doubled-concentration regimen in twenty-nine Mexico City patients delivered the landmark clinical result reported by IPN: one hundred percent HPV elimination in every woman who carried HPV without premalignant lesions. Among Mexico City women who entered the cohort already harboring both HPV infection and premalignant cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, the non-invasive therapy cleared pathology in 64.3 percent of cases, while resolving 57.2 percent of premalignant lesions lacking detectable HPV—with zero collateral injury to healthy vaginal or uterine tissue: Clinical Modality / Cohort Target Patient Group Mechanism of Action Documented Efficacy & Structural Outcome IPN Phase I: Oaxaca & Veracruz (n = 420) Women with HPV and/or premalignant CIN lesions Standard-dose topical 5-ALA + 3 red-laser sessions (48 h apart) 85% HPV clearance (HPV-only & HPV+lesions); zero cervical scarring IPN Phase II: Mexico City Cohort (n = 29) Urban cohort with HPV only, HPV+CIN, or CIN alone Doubled 5-ALA concentration + 2 cycles spaced 48 hours apart 100% clearance in lesion-free HPV carriers; 64.3% in HPV+lesions LEEP / Cold-Knife Conization Persistent high-grade dysplasia (CIN 2 / CIN 3) Electrosurgical wire or scalpel excision of cervical tissue cone 85–95% lesion removal, but shortens cervix and raises preterm birth risk Cervical Cryotherapy / Thermal Ablation Selected low-to-moderate ectocervical lesions Non-selective freezing or heat necrosis of surface mucosa 75–88% ablation; risk of cervical stenosis and missed deep crypt virus Prophylactic HPV Vaccination (L1 VLP) Adolescents & young adults prior to viral exposure Neutralizing antibodies blocking initial viral capsid entry >90% prevention of new HPV-16/18 infections; cannot clear existing HPV PCR Molecular Verification and Co-Pathogen Clearance Polymerase chain reaction assays verified true molecular absence of high-risk HPV DNA. Crucially, ENCB-IPN researchers refused to declare viral eradication based solely on cleaner microscopic Pap smears or visual colposcopy. Because subclinical viral episomes can linger silently inside deep basal keratinocytes long after surface koilocytes disappear, her laboratory paired cytopathology with sensitive polymerase chain reaction amplification targeting conserved L1 and E6/E7 viral sequences. Confirming negative post-treatment PCR assays across one hundred percent of the lesion-free HPV carriers in Mexico City proved that singlet-oxygen photochemistry paired with local Langerhans and cytotoxic T-cell recruitment drove viral genomes below molecular detection thresholds. Parallel microbiological testing across the cohort uncovered an equally practical clinical bonus for women’s reproductive health. Chronic cervicovaginal co-infections damage epithelial tight junctions, deplete protective lactobacilli, and generate nitrosative inflammation that accelerates high-risk HPV DNA integration into host chromosomes. In IPN’s evaluations, topical 5-ALA photodynamic therapy simultaneously cleared 81 percent of concurrent pathogenic bacterial infections—including Chlamydia trachomatis—and 80 percent of Candida albicans fungal infections, restoring balanced mucosal immunity. Complementary Prevention Alongside Global HPV Vaccination Dr. Ramón Gallegos’s laboratory continues training a new generation of Mexican women scientists. Public-health oncologists emphasize that non-invasive photodynamic therapy complements rather than replaces childhood HPV vaccination and routine molecular cervical screening. While prophylactic L1 virus-like particle vaccines remain extraordinarily effective at blocking initial viral entry prior to exposure, vaccine-induced serum antibodies cannot enter basal keratinocytes to clear persistent HPV infections acquired years earlier. For the hundreds of millions of adult women worldwide already living with persistent high-risk HPV—especially in regions where surgical oncology specialists are scarce—an outpatient light-activated therapy bridges the gap between primary vaccination and invasive surgery. Combining vaccination, molecular screening, and non-invasive therapy protects generations of women. Ongoing translational goals for biophotonics researchers in Mexico and abroad include larger multicenter randomized Phase III trials, portable medical LED cervical illuminators suited for rural community clinics, and affordable generic 5-ALA gels. supplementary_news.content_title: 罕见!年轻女孩同时感染18种HPV亚型|HPV 疫苗:第一针是启动,第二针才筑牢保护!
supplementary_news.content: 为 近日,杭州临平区妇幼保健院接诊了这一则特殊病例。女孩外阴疼痛就诊,最终确诊外阴尖锐湿疣, HPV检测一次性检出18种亚型阳性,其中包含 10 种高危亚型。接诊医生称该病例十分罕见。 HPV检验报告/医院供图 接诊医生介绍, 女孩 来杭探亲,半个月来外阴隐隐疼痛,总觉得有异物感,最近难受得越来越厉害,正常生活都受影响。专科查体发现其外阴长了典型的菜花状赘生物,从外观来看很像尖锐湿疣。为了查清到底感染了哪些病毒,医生给她做了高精度 HPV分型检测,结果让人意外: 一共查出 18种HPV亚型同时阳性,感染的亚型多、病毒载量很高。 HPV分型检测/医院供图 值得高度警惕的是,在 18种阳性亚型中,包含10种高危致癌型HPV,是诱发宫颈上皮内病变甚至进展为宫颈癌的核心风险亚型。一次性多重混合感染18种亚型 且高危占比极高,提示患者病毒暴露时间长、感染复杂、远期癌变风险显著升高。接诊医生结合女孩的症状、专科体征及精准 HPV分型结果,最终确诊为外阴尖锐湿疣、HPV多重高危感染,目前正在积极治疗中。 展开全文 科普延伸 HPV 也就是人乳头瘤病毒,传播途径不只有 性接触,潮湿公共环境、皮肤微小破损也可能造成间接感染,抓挠还会造成病毒自身扩散 。 HPV亚型众多,低危型多引发各类疣体,包括丝状疣、跖疣、尖锐湿疣等;高危型以16、18型风险最高,持续感染可诱发宫颈癌等肿瘤,早期大多没有症状。 低危型 HPV感染:皮肤或生殖器长疣 低危型 HPV本身没有致癌基因,它引起的多是良性的疣体增生,癌变风险较低。它一般出现在 眼睛周围、手背、前臂 等部位,有米粒至黄豆大小,扁平微微鼓起的小丘疹,数目较多且密集, 颜色起初呈肉或粉色 ,时间久了,还会变成深褐色,会有瘙痒感。 高危型 HPV:早期无声息,后期有肿块 典型代表就是 HPV16型、18型 !致癌性最强,有约 70%的宫颈癌是由这两种HPV病毒引起的,还可能引发外阴癌、肛门癌、口咽癌等多种癌症,还有HPV31型、33型、45型、52型、58型等14种,致癌风险都很高。不过,它们早期通常无症状,到后期才可能出现异常阴道出血、白带异常、局部肿块、小腹坠胀等症状。 定期筛查 +接种疫苗有助降低HPV风险 所以,定期筛查格外重要,建议大家可以去医院做 HPV检测,至少五年一次,还可以做TCT(宫颈脱落细胞学)检查,至少三年一次。 此外,还可以选择接种疫苗,来帮助预防感染 HPV病毒。 去年11月10日起,HPV疫苗正式纳入国家免疫规划,2011年11月10日以后出生、满13周岁的适龄女生有权利和义务免费接种二价HPV疫苗。 HPV疫苗能有效预防子宫颈癌等疾病,为花季少女筑牢青春健康屏障,守护她们的成长。可能有的家长犹豫说:“我的孩子还小,等长大了再打也来得及。”但其实, 初中阶段是接种 HPV疫苗的黄金期:防护效果更好,青春期免疫系统活跃,接种后产生的抗体水平比成年后的水平更高,保护力更强。预防大于一切。17-24岁是我国女性感染HPV病毒的第一个高峰时期,提前接种,能在暴露风险来临前,为孩子筑牢健康屏障。 大家快行动起来,成功预约、按时接种 HPV疫苗。但这里有一个非常普遍的误区: 打上第一针 ≠有完整保护,第一针是免疫启动,第二针才是巩固抗体、拉高保护水平的核心! 同时还要记住两个核心真相: HPV疫苗是预防性疫苗,没有治疗作用。对已经存在的 HPV 感染、已经发生的病变,无法清除;无论二价、四价、九价,只能覆盖对应亚型,疫苗不能替代定期 HPV+TCT 筛查。就算全程打完疫苗,适龄女性依然要按时筛查。 上述罕见的多重 HPV 感染病例,不是制造焦虑,而是提醒我们: HPV的病毒亚型繁多,感染风险真实存在。想防护,优先尽早接种HPV疫苗;约上、打上第一针,只是第一步;按时打卡第二针,完成规范剂次,才能拿到更可靠的保护。 你已经打上 HPV 第一针了吗?记得设置提醒,按时接种下一针!具体接种间隔、剂次,以门诊医生、疫苗说明书为准;如果错过第二针时间,不需要从头重打,尽快前往接种门诊补齐即可。 供 稿 | 马欢欢 初 审 | 马欢欢 复 审 | 王立博 终 审 | 布仁巴图 通辽市疾病预防控制中心 Tongliao Center for Diseases Prevention and Control 关爱健康公卫先行 预防疾病健康通辽 返回搜狐,查看更多

AMCP Nexus 2026| HSES 2026 Advertisement News|Articles|November 20, 2026 For transgender women with HIV, risk awareness and provider trust shape anal cancer follow-up Author(s)Logan Lutton Listen 0:00 / 5:10 Key Takeaways Transgender women experience markedly higher anal cancer prevalence, driven by high-risk anal HPV, with HIV acting as a major cofactor that increases HSIL risk independent of viral suppression or ART use. Consensus guidance recommends screening transgender women with HIV starting at 35 years and without HIV at 45 years, reflecting incidence >70/100,000 person-years in key HIV-affected populations. Follow-through after abnormal cytology is suboptimal; prior data show high referral rates to HRA but less than half completing the procedure, representing a preventable oncologic care gap. Confusion between cytology, HRA, and colonoscopy, plus emotional and physical discomfort, impede adherence; step-by-step explanations and supportive clinician behaviors mitigate distress. Gender-affirming, trusted providers strongly influence uptake, and community support plus HPV-focused education, correct pronoun use, and self-collected sampling could improve completion rates. SHOW MORE Among 16 Black transgender women, 15 with HIV, risk awareness, comfort, provider trust and support shaped whether they completed HRA, according to a new qualitative study. Advertisement Transgender women face an anal cancer prevalence 5.5 times higher than cisgender individuals, a gap the researchers linked largely to high rates of anal high-risk HPV infection. For transgender women living with HIV, knowing that the virus raises their anal cancer risk can push them toward follow-up care, but gaps in screening knowledge, discomfort with the procedure and limited trust in clinicians can still stand in the way, according to the results of a recent qualitative study published in JoVE Journal. The study was led by a team of researchers, including senior author Darren Whitfield, Ph.D., an associate professor at the University of Maryland School of Social Work. Whitfield and his team included semi-structured interviews with 16 Black transgender women who had abnormal anal cytology and were referred for high-resolution anoscopy (HRA), which detects and treats high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL), the precursor to anal cancer. Half had completed HRA and half had not. Participants were recruited from a clinic that offers gender-affirming care, and most were 35 or older (81%), stably housed (81%) and living with HIV (94%). How HIV raises anal cancer risk for transgender women Transgender women face an anal cancer prevalence 5.5 times higher than cisgender individuals, a gap the researchers linked largely to high rates of anal high-risk of human papillomavirus (HPV). The authors described HIV as the second most important risk factor in this population. HIV potentiates HPV infection and raises the likelihood of HSIL regardless of viral suppression or antiretroviral therapy use. That overlap matters because HIV is concentrated among transgender women. In CDC’s National HIV Behavioral Surveillance of 1,608 transgender women in seven U.S. cities, 42% received a positive HIV test result. The International Anal Neoplasia Society’s 2024 consensus guidelines recommend that transgender women with HIV begin screening at age 35 and those without HIV at age 45. The earlier start reflects an incidence of more than 70 per 100,000 person-years among transgender women and men who have sex with men with HIV, according to an ASCCP practice advisory. The first U.S. anal cancer screening guidelines for people with HIV followed later that year, according to the National Cancer Institute. Recommendations tailored to you Sign in or create an account to see articles, videos, and podcasts matched to your specialties. Sign in or sign up Follow-through after an abnormal result remains a weak point. In an earlier cohort of 75 transgender women, 49% had abnormal cytology. Of those, 89% were referred to HRA, but only 47% completed it. “This highlights a potential missed opportunity to prevent anal cancer in this population at elevated risk for cancer,” Whitfield and his team wrote in the study. How HIV awareness affects HRA decisions Several participants said knowing their HIV status raised their anal cancer risk factored into their decision. “Being that I’m HIV-positive, that it must be addressed immediately,” said one participant, though she had not completed HRA herself. Still, many could not distinguish anal cytology from HRA or from colonoscopy. Comfort also played a role. Some participants felt emotionally vulnerable having a clinician collect the anal swab, and most who completed HRA reported discomfort that eased when providers explained each step. Provider trust in HIV and gender-affirming care Participants who described positive relationships with clinicians were more willing to follow recommendations. One participant who completed HRA said the specialist her primary care doctor referred her to “made it feel at ease.” Others said they preferred to rely on a physician they already knew, and a lack of affirming communication was cited as a barrier. Whitfield and his team wrote that raising HRA completion may depend on encouragement from providers who serve and are trusted by transgender women. Prior research cited in the paper found an odds ratio of 241.57 for completing anal cytology among transgender individuals when a provider recommended the test. Why HPV gets less attention than HIV among transgender women Participants said anal health is rarely discussed in their community, where HIV has long been the focus. “HIV was the higher thing people was scared to talk about and talk to. It wasn’t about HPV,” said one participant who completed HRA. Others said lacking support kept them away. “If I find out I have something, who do I have to cry to? Nobody,” said one participant who did not complete HRA. The authors recommended gender-neutral HPV education inclusive of transgender women, consistent use of preferred names and pronouns, opportunities for self-collected anal cytology and integration of social support networks into screening programs. They noted the sample came from a single clinic with an existing research partnership and that all participants had healthcare access. Asked what would help more transgender women complete HRA, one participant who did not complete the procedure said providers “should say more caring [things]. Be more compassionate about the things that trans women go through.” Newsletter Get the latest industry news, event updates and more from Managed Healthcare Executive. supplementary_news.content: Oncologists Urge Adults 45 and Under to Get the HPV Vaccine for Cancer Prevention Modern medicine has made it so that a cancer diagnosis is no longer a death sentence. For instance, survival rates of breast and ovarian cancer have risen, giving us more time to live a life with love. Oncologists are grateful for advances like mammograms to screen for breast cancer, and chemotherapy and radiation to fight the disease. Still, no one would wish a cancer diagnosis on themselves or a loved one. "Treatment still takes a significant physical, emotional and financial toll on patients," Dr. Gabrielle Smith, MD, a gynecologic oncologist with HonorHealth, explains to Parade. "Preventing cancer whenever possible is so important, as it can spare someone that entire experience." She knows we can't control every risk factor for cancer. You may not have had control over a work environment that exposed you to toxic chemicals, for example, and you certainly didn't willingly "sign up" to have certain genetics. Still, as a gynecologic oncologist, Dr. Smith wants people to know all of their options because she doesn't want them to become her patients. Staying up to date or catching up with certain vaccines is one way to lower your risk of certain cancers. "All cancers are diseases of our genes, and sometimes a virus can alter or hijack our genes, which eventually leads to cancer," Dr. Smith says. "When we vaccinate against a known virus that can cause cancer, we have an opportunity to interrupt that process before it starts." Vaccines aren't "just for kids," and flu and COVID-19 shots aren't the only ones available to adults in their 20s, 30s and 40s. For this reason, oncologists urge adults 45 and under to ask about one vaccine in particular, as it could protect them from several cancers. 🩺SIGN UP for Parade's health newsletter with expert-approved tips, healthy eats, exercises, news & more to help you stay healthy & feel your best self💊 Oncologists Are Begging Adults 45 and Under to Ask About This Vaccine Oncologists urge people 45 and under to get the HPV vaccine because it can protect you against six types of cancer: Cervical, oropharyngeal (throat), anal, vulvar, vaginal and penile. The HPV vaccine can stop "the underlying viral infection that causes" these cancers, says Dr. Ami Vaidya, MD, co-chief of the Division of Gynecologic Oncology at the Hackensack Meridian John Theurer Cancer Center. The FDA approved the first HPV vaccine in 2006, and it targeted four variants of human papillomavirus (HPV), a virus that commonly spreads through sexual contact. In 2014, the FDA approved the Gardasil 9 HPV vaccine, which doctors still use today. Dr. Vaidya says it targets nine high-risk viral strains of HPV. Doctors recommend the HPV vaccine to all children ages 11–12 (but children can begin getting the vaccination at age nine). It's a two-dose series for ages 9–14. However, people can receive a three-dose series up to age 45. "The vaccine is made with the outer coating of the virus to teach your immune system to recognize the virus and create antibodies that can then destroy the virus if you are exposed to it in the future, before it causes an infection," Dr. Smith says. "Since the vaccine does not contain any DNA from the virus, you cannot get infected with HPV from the vaccine." Related: 'I'm an Oncologist—This Is the First Symptom I'd Never Ignore in Someone Under 40′ Why Do Oncologists Recommend the HPV Vaccine to People Ages 27-45? The recommended age for the HPV vaccine is 11-12 years, but people can receive their first dose at age 9. Doctors and medical organizations like the CDC continue to recommend the HPV vaccine for people ages 13-26 (the "catch-up" demographic). However, Dr. Vaidya encourages people to ask about the vaccine up to and including age 45, saying the vaccine remains "highly beneficial" for many people. It provides robust protection against any of the nine high-risk viral strains a person has not yet encountered," Dr. Vaidya says. "This is especially crucial for individuals experiencing life transitions—such as re-entering the dating pool after a breakup or divorce—which introduce new opportunities for exposure." She adds that natural HPV infections don't always give you lasting immunity, so the vaccine offers a "much stronger antibody response" that can guard you against reinfection, lower your long-term health risks like throat cancer and protect future partners from transmission. Related: 'I Was Diagnosed With Cancer at 16 and Again at 39—These Were the Very First Symptoms I Noticed' Dr. Vaidya says there's no approved HPV vaccine for people ages 46 and older because many people in this age group were already exposed to the virus during sexual activity. "Immunization can only prevent new infections, not treat or clear existing ones," she says. Dr. Vaidya adds that HPV is a slow-acting virus and usually takes one to three decades of persistent infection to progress to cancer. "A new infection acquired later in life is much less likely to develop into cancer within a person's natural lifespan," she says. But if you're 45 and under, Drs. Vaidya and Smith agree that it's worth asking your doctor about the HPV vaccine. "Health experts recommend 'shared clinical decision-making,' meaning adults should consult with their doctor to determine if vaccination aligns with their current lifestyle and personal risk factors," she says. Up Next: Related: The Lung Cancer Screening Oncologists Say Almost No One Eligible Gets (But Should) Sources: - Dr. Ami Vaidya, MD, the co-chief of the Division of Gynecologic Oncology at the Hackensack Meridian John Theurer Cancer Center - Dr. Gabrielle Smith, MD, a gynecologic oncologist with HonorHealth - Survival Rates for Breast Cancer. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 21, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer Dual Molecular Assays Show Strong Agreement for Cervical Cancer Screening in Cameroon by November 20, 2026 in Cancer Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Dual Molecular Assays Show Strong Agreement for Cervical Cancer Screening in Cameroon Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Researchers evaluating primary cervical cancer screening strategies in Cameroon have demonstrated high diagnostic concordance between two widely available commercial molecular platforms detecting high-risk oncogenic human papillomavirus. In a cross-sectional study analyzing endocervical swab samples from adult women, investigators compared the analytical performance of the Abbott RealTime High Risk human papillomavirus assay performed on the m2000rt instrument with the Sacace HPV Genotypes 14 Real-TM Quant assay executed on the QuantStudio 7 Flex platform. The findings, reported in Infectious Agents and Cancer, reveal a Cohen kappa coefficient of 0.800 between the systems, establishing that these multiplex molecular platforms can operate interoperably within resource-constrained national healthcare frameworks seeking to expand cervical screening access. Cervical cancer represents a severe public health burden in Cameroon, where model estimates indicate that approximately 2,770 women receive a cervical cancer diagnosis annually and 1,787 women die from the malignancy. Although the World Health Organization has established global elimination targets for 2030 that require screening 70 percent of adult women with high-performance molecular assays by age 35 and 45, Cameroon currently lacks a standardized national screening algorithm or systematic government screening program. Existing testing initiatives have largely remained sporadic, driven predominantly by civil society organizations and clinical research institutions. Expanding screening coverage has encountered structural hurdles due to the high capital expense of deploying dedicated molecular testing instruments across decentralized regional hospitals, prompting researchers to assess whether existing infrastructure can be repurposed. To address this diagnostic gap, investigators leveraged molecular laboratory instruments originally distributed across Cameroon for other public health priorities. While centralized reference facilities have maintained Abbott platforms for decades to support human immunodeficiency virus viral load quantification, decentralized regional treatment centres received open QuantStudio 7 Flex real-time polymerase chain reaction instruments during emergency laboratory expansions for SARS-CoV-2 testing. Because these multi-pathogen platforms remain underutilized following the acute phase of the coronavirus pandemic, establishing the analytical comparability of assays running on these distinct instruments provides an empirical pathway to scale decentralized cervical screening without requiring prohibitive procurement of new closed-system machinery. Discover more Research assistant services Learn Engineering Track Biotech Tour Colleges Cancer research funding The study protocol recruited 364 adult female participants aged 18 years and older who presented for cervicovaginal screening between April and November 2023 at two major metropolitan tertiary healthcare facilities: the Gynaeco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital of Yaounde and the Gynaeco-Obstetric and Pediatric Hospital of Douala. Sample size determination utilized Cochran’s formula based on an anticipated national human papillomavirus prevalence of 20.9 percent reported in International Agency for Research on Cancer statistical registries, requiring a minimum enrollment threshold of 254 individuals. The participant cohort exhibited a median age of 41 years, with an interquartile range extending from 34 to 50 years, closely matching the target demographic recognized to carry higher vulnerability to invasive cervical malignancy. Specimen collection followed standardized operating protocols utilizing Abbott Cervi-Collect specimen collection devices, with swabs preserved in PreservCyt medium and stored in cryo-racks at minus 80 degrees Celsius before batch processing at the Chantal Biya International Reference Centre for research on HIV/AIDS prevention and care in Yaounde. For the Abbott assay, automated nucleic acid extraction was executed with 400-microliter input volumes on the m2000sp instrument, followed by real-time fluorescent probe amplification on the m2000rt system to detect genotypes 16 and 18 individually alongside a pooled detection channel covering twelve additional high-risk viral types. Comparative analysis with the Sacace assay extracted genomic material from 200-microliter samples using QIAamp DNA Mini kits prior to multiplex amplification identifying 14 specific high-risk genotypes individually. Discover more Donate to Research Find Conferences Health Initial diagnostic screening of the 364 enrolled participants revealed overall high-risk human papillomavirus positivity rates of 21.4 percent, representing 78 positive samples, using the Abbott platform, compared to 15.4 percent, or 56 positive samples, using the Sacace platform. Cross-tabulation demonstrated a positive concordance of 72 percent, with 56 samples concordantly positive across both platforms, and a negative concordance of 93 percent, reflecting 286 samples confirmed negative by both diagnostic systems. The observed statistical agreement yielded a Cohen kappa value of 0.800 with a 95 percent confidence interval spanning from 0.721 to 0.879, meeting the defined criteria for strong diagnostic agreement between independent multiplex diagnostic technologies. To resolve analytical discrepancies, investigators subjected all 22 discordant specimens—each testing positive by Abbott but negative by Sacace—to independent secondary arbitration using the Anyplex II HPV28 genotyping kit, which simultaneously identifies 19 high-risk and 9 low-risk types. Arbitration analysis confirmed the presence of high-risk viral sequences in 19 of the 22 discordant specimens, or 86.36 percent, while only three samples retained complete undetectability. Following arbitration, the verified cumulative prevalence of high-risk human papillomavirus infection in the studied cohort reached 20.6 percent, corresponding to 75 confirmed positive individuals. Authors noted that analytical discordance stemmed primarily from divergent analytical detection limits, as Sacace thresholds report viral loads around 1,000 genomic equivalents per 100,000 cells, whereas Abbott captures lower viral concentrations. Genotypic discrimination conducted across confirmed cases identified 12 circulating high-risk oncogenic types in the cohort, with genotypes 31 and 51 remaining completely undetected. Among positive isolates, human papillomavirus genotype 16 appeared most frequently, representing 18.8 percent of detected infections, followed closely by genotype 18 at 16.0 percent, genotype 39 at 16.0 percent, and genotype 58 at 13.0 percent. The prominent detection of genotypes 39 and 58 highlights localized genetic diversity that contrasts with historical surveys among female sex workers in Cameroon, where genotypes 51, 53, and 52 predominated, as well as cytological cohorts in Yaounde that observed higher relative frequencies of genotype 45 alongside types 16 and 18. A comparative health-economic analysis conducted by the investigators identified critical structural trade-offs between consumable costs and platform capital requirements. Reagent expenses alone favored the Abbott assay, which demonstrated an operating reagent cost of approximately 11.82 United States dollars per test, compared to 23.36 dollars per test for the Sacace assay, representing a 50.6 percent lower consumable cost per individual examination. However, deploying new proprietary Abbott instruments across peripheral healthcare centers requires substantial capital investments that regional budgets cannot support. Because public regional hospitals across Cameroon already possess functional QuantStudio 7 Flex instruments, utilizing these decentralized open systems allows health authorities to bypass capital procurement expenses, offsetting higher unit reagent costs through local multi-pathogen testing efficiency. Synthesizing their diagnostic and economic findings, the researchers proposed a standardized operational screening algorithm tailored for resource-limited settings. Under this strategic framework, reference laboratories equipped with existing Abbott systems continue high-throughput primary screening utilizing the assay’s superior analytical sensitivity and lower reagent expenses, while peripheral regional facilities utilize open QuantStudio instruments to deliver accessible frontline detection and comprehensive genotypic discrimination. The authors noted that a primary limitation of their evaluation involved comparing only two proprietary assay chemistries, emphasizing that future research should examine broader panels of commercial reagents to further refine interoperable screening protocols across sub-Saharan Africa. Detailed clinical examination and sociodemographic profiling of the study cohort offered broader insights into screening-seeking behavior among Cameroonian women. Beyond age distributions, clinical assessments revealed that 68.4 percent of participants, representing 249 women, presented with normal vaginal discharges and no demonstrable cervical inflammation. Mild cervical inflammation occurred in 15.4 percent (56 women), moderate inflammation was documented in another 15.4 percent (56 women), and only 0.8 percent (three women) presented with severe cervical inflammation. Educational attainment within the cohort was substantial, with 84.9 percent having completed at least secondary-level schooling. Regarding reproductive and behavioral history, 79.9 percent reported their sexual debut occurred before age 20, 62.1 percent were married, divorced, or widowed, and 59.1 percent recorded a history of two to six pregnancies. The authors observed that the high proportion of asymptomatic women presenting without inflammation demonstrates meaningful public awareness and voluntary participation in preventive screening despite the absence of an organized national program. Beyond aggregate positivity, concordance between the two test kits was further mapped across five distinct high-risk viral diagnostic categories. Among the 78 positive specimens detected by Abbott, eleven samples tested positive solely for genotype 16, six specimens were positive exclusively for genotype 18, two contained genotype 16 alongside other high-risk types, three carried genotype 18 with other types, and 56 fell into the pooled other high-risk category. Discrepancies in the detection of different or identical genotypes proved most prominent for HPV 18, occurring in six of nine discordant evaluations. Methodological controls maintained strict data integrity throughout the study, including ethical clearance from the Regional Ethics Committee and written assent from all participants. The researchers also contextualized their findings within broader international challenges in molecular cervical screening. According to global inventories, between 50 percent and 79 percent of more than 250 commercially available molecular assays lack peer-reviewed publications or sufficient evidence demonstrating their analytical performance quality. While other platforms present in Cameroon, including Cobas and GeneXpert systems, identify high-risk infections, they do not provide the detailed genotypic discrimination enabled by the QuantStudio platform. Establishing rigorous local interoperability between existing instruments therefore provides a verified foundation for standardized national screening guidelines.
